review_text:
Excellently prepared meal with unique flavors.

We stopped by with a reservation on a Friday evening, and it was pretty quiet meal given that I think it was still its first week and there was definitely space for more tables. There are too many dishes to recount in detail, but all of the ingredients were extremely fresh (although a bit lacking in protein). Among the more memorable dishes included the Maine shrimp, the king crab, the squid tart, and the dry aged rib eye; the latter in particular was an amazingly tender and flavorful piece of meat. We also split a wine pairing between my friend and I, and they poured it into two glasses for us so that we could share both, which I greatly appreciated.

Overall, it's a pricey but excellent place for a quiet, refined, not very heavy meal with excellent flavors.

Congrats!
Michelin 2* & Michelin's best new restaurant in NYC.

Never been to the original Aska, which received numerous accolades from prominent food critics and a Michelin star.
Executive Chef Fredrik Berselius just opened up his Nordic restaurant in another location right across Williamsburg Bridge. You can just walk across the bridge, and the restaurant is right there.

Left very, very impressed; Overall, wonderful tasting menu (18-courses) from beginning to end.

Highlights:  All (Not going into details; Very creative & delicious, some using unique techniques & preparation).
You just have to come & try it yourself. 
= Culinary genius

Excellent wine pairing (& reasonably priced).

Impeccable service. Wonderful/very friendly staff.
Chef Berselius came by the table often.
Big thumbs up for playing some great tunes from The Smiths (Arghhh.......I'm so old.). 

Gratuity included. No tipping here.

Highest recommendation.

: 10 calendars

Note:  They also have a casual outdoor dining area (with separate, inexpensive, but limited a la carte menu) - no reservations required for that one - and a bar downstairs.

Ahhh... Aska is back! The original Aska, a small space in the back of Kinfolk Studios, was on our top 3 tasting menus in New York City. We were greatly saddened when it closed in 2014, but have been waiting patiently for chef Fredrik Berselius's reopening. We dined at Aska opening week, and the menu did not disappoint! Fortunately for us, opening week also fell on our 7-year anniversary, so we made it an occasion. 

The restaurant is right by the Williamsburg Bridge with quite an unassuming storefront; use to be an old warehouse. When we checked in with the hostess, we were led downstairs to a cellar bar and poured a glass of champagne in celebration of our anniversary. It was a lovely gesture. While we enjoyed a toast, we noticed that the bar serves a more casual a la carte menu as well as wine, beer, and cocktails. As far as I'm aware, they don't take reservations for the bar (or garden); it's first come first served.

We were then led back upstairs to the main dining room. Gorgeous space. It was dark and moody, but spacious and intimate with an open kitchen. We didn't do a pairing with our tasting menu, but we ordered 2 cocktails each throughout our dining, which were as superb as you would imagine. The tasting menu consisted of 19 courses, each dish was beautifully curated--visually and taste-wise. Each ingredient is deliberate, and Chef Berselius has foraged some (most?) of it himself. An innovative culinary journey. To give a sense of the menu, I will bore you with the details of some of the highlights: 
CAVIAR: grilled onion, sustainable finish caviar from Carelian, cultured cream, lemon verbena
RAZOR CLAM: razor claim, peas, elderflower and while pea oil
BLOOD PANCAKE: blood pancake, cherry, rose and rosehip
SKATE: cured skate wing, celery root puree with its leaves, roasted celery root, unfiltered rapeseed oil and flowering dill
SQUID TART: tart made with seaweed, charred squid and a puree made from dulse
BEEF: 50 day dry aged rib eye, preserved black currant and salted plum from last year, cured beef fat

And there were 3 delicious, fresh desserts! 

The entire experience was about 3 hours. Service was orderly and flawless. The tasting menu is completely and thoroughly worth it. It came as a surprise that at the end of the meal, we learned that tax and gratuity were already included in the price. 

Outstanding meal and evening! Aska remains one of my top favorite tasting menus in NYC, and I'm excited and appreciate that there is an a la carte dining option now. I hope to be back again soon!

What a great experience at this newly opened Williamsburg restaurant. The chef is a genius. The food was outstanding. The restaurant space is great. We were brought downstairs for a drink in the lounge before being shown to our table. They have a nice garden space too. The tables themselves are beautiful wood. The kitchen is open so you can see the master at work. 

I love the new Nordic/Scandinavian cuisine, after a trip to Scandinavia last year. The forward thinking and pushing the boundaries of innovation continually amazes me. We had a 20 course culinary journey. I think I didn't care for one dish. Beyond that they were all very good to fantastic. The plating was stunning. The highlights for me were the langoustine, the oysters, the liken with mushroom, and the strawberry dessert. 

The chef is a humble and kind guy who spent time talking to us during dinner and afterward.  The staff was all very friendly and informative. 

Obviously full after 20 courses but not stuffed. My friends may disagree. I just had a great time. Not an every day restaurant. But definitely worth the splurge. They also have a bar menu in the garden and lounge that doesn't require a reservation. Can't wait to go back. And oh, there's a cool parting gift.

The chefs delivered an icredible dining experience bolstered by an excellent team of waiters/hosts. 

I didnt particularly enjoy every single dish (2 I didn't like) however every individual course was truly unique, regardless of my satisfaction. Can go into extreme detail for each course but that would be corny as hell. True to every dish were the various layers of flavors, even in a single bite. Some don't even hit till you begin your second bite, then you go hey... 

Waitstaff was incredibly attentive and friendly, was trying to think about something to write and just realized I don't even remember them clearing out the plates and cutlery between each course. Do remember the setting of cutlery and the presentation of each course, very theatrical, however the transition between each act, very ninja-esque.

Dinner is pre-paid when you make a reservation, so there is an added bonus of feeling like the meal was free. Btw totally worth the price if you don't feel the freebie-ness of it.

Lastly, don't plan anything too close to your reservation time, dinner took us a little over 4 hours. A quick 4, not the draggy kinda 4

Bar review only. My wife and I went to the bar downstairs on a Thursday night. It was an amazing experience and we cannot wait to go back. The atmosphere is incredible, like hanging out in a friend's amazing Scandinavian den with cool music and great food. We sat on a couch and they brought two of the best cocktails we have ever had. They were complex, light, and beautiful - hard to describe but if you love cocktails like we do, you must try the Edda, a great gin based drink. 

The bar manager came over and she even gave us cold shots of the Black Death, Iceland's Brennivin. A gem of a bar for South Williamsburg!

Frederik Berselius is keeping Williamsburg incredible.
My heartfelt dining experience is from how genuine Aska is: from food, staff, services, ambience, space. 

Food- They truly speaks for themselves.  Frederick is so talented, the food absolutely lives up to the hype and more. I was able to recognize familiar ingredients as well as exotic Scandinavian dishes that was completely mind-blowing (ie: blood pancake? SO GOOD.) 

Staff & Service - I loved how Frederick was able personally come table-side to EVERY one of the tables during service.  It was another high point to see the artists at work right in front of me!

Ambience & Space - The best way to describe the setting might be a dark theater or gallery with spot lights directly in the kitchen.  Very very interesting play of space, I felt I was part of an audiences watching a big production unfold.  

Frederik took my boyfriend and I to the downstairs bar area after our meal and we chatted casually about our experiences and he spoke to us about his idea to make the downstairs bar as a neighborhood place.  
I can't say I've had a similar experience dining anywhere else in the past.  It was high-end, yet artistic, yet neighborhoody. This place is sincerely incredible.

In a nutshell, Aska is very similar to Aquavit, where food is presented more with its originality (though many times preservation is required), and less with cooking techniques. Having said that, the flavor did taste rather unique for many courses we had tried.

Hits and misses: I did like the oyster and caviar - both were marinated to perfection and had carried a fresh and light taste; that 120-day rib-eye was so tender and juicy that I could literally feel it melt down on my tongue. The blood pancake was rather disappointing - probably I am just not that into blood-made food, that the complex flavor was a bit disturbing to me. Our chef was extremely considerate and replaced my friend's pancake with a regular one, after her communication with the waiter. Very well done! 

Overall this dinner to me was well-executed, a bit less complicated and more open-ended. Scandinavian food was certainly nowhere top on my list, yet Aska did breakthrough and I view it as one of the strongest candidates for the new Michelin star family.

I had heard great things about chef Fredrik Berselius, but had never been to one of his restaurants, nor have I had Scandinavian food, so I was super excited to try out his newest space. 

The short: this is an amazing dining experience all around - food & alcohol, ambiance and service. I highly recommend the tasting menu.

The longer: we hopped out of an Uber in front of a sleek black building. We arrived a bit early, because we wanted to check out the downstairs bar. It was beautiful -- dimly lit, cozy furnishings, and beautifully decorated with upside down dried flowers and exposed brick. We tried both of the gin cocktails and loved them. 

We did the 10 course tasting menu with the beverage pairing. I'm by no means a food connoisseur (I grew up in an Italian household eating meatballs and chicken cutlets), so I was excited to try a new cuisine and different kinds of food. 

What I loved: the aged prime rib was ridiculously amazing, the oysters & caviar were incredible, the bread basket with the special butters was addictive, and the cured skate wing was unreal. 

What I tried, but might not eat again: blood pancake and the blood mignardise (dessert truffle). The blood was a unique flavor, but a little too crazy for me. 

The waiters, waitresses, and chefs were all so awesome and attentive; the space is open, yet intimate and totally beautiful; and it was an incredible experience overall. I highly recommend it! :)

It was a very memorable dining experience and perfect for a special occasion. We arrived early and had a drink at the bar downstairs. Simple and relaxing decor. If I lived in the neighborhood it'd be my favorite hangout for sure. The drinks of course were unique and very fit for the ambience. Once in the dining room I was impressed with the extremely generous table positioning. In addition we were told the table was ours all evening to enjoy the 19 course meal without a rush. The flow and pacing of the course was perfect and I did not feel overstuffed at the end of the meal as I had feared. The food was extremely creative and interesting as expected. I wouldn't compare to Aquavit as each has own unique character. With the excellent food and flawless service we were truly entertained for four short hours.

every course was absolutely delicious!!!! every broth, reduction, sauce was simply devine and made every dish over-the-top flavorful!!!!! this restaurant is a gem!!!!! and one of the staff members suggested another restaurant to try for breakfast (Okonomi) which I went to as well, and it was UNREAL!!!!!!

We went in October. It was her 30th birthday. We were met with warm smiles from everyone. They all made it a point to congratulate us. The character of the restaurant is given breath by the simple and unique culture of the staff. They are a well oiled machine and have done their homework. They are passionate about their focus. They are a family. 

This was our second time to Aska. Fredrik Berselius and the Aska family provided an incredible experience, from beginning to end, that will be a lifetime memory. From the first steps in, we felt taken care of. 

The design of the entire space is clean and elegant and dark. It felt right; cohesive with depth. The upstairs dining layout is spacious and well suited to ensure that you can focus on you. The kitchen is exposed offering a glimpse at the artists at work. There is also an outdoor space

We kicked things off at the downstairs bar, enjoying delicious cocktails and the attention commanding decor. We returned upstairs to our table and the 10-course symphony began. I could talk for days about each dish but I am going to pass. I suppose it's more important to tell that Chef Berselius' vision has matured and extends throughout each dish to create a comprehensive, connected experience. It was one plate of genius after another bringing flavors, textures, colors, and contrasts that I have never explored. It was beautiful. The product is there and it is art. 

This will be a yearly visit for sure.

To be fare, I should probably give it 3.5-4 stars for all the good things on those dishes. However, the service was so bad, that I am still pissed. 

The service charge was included in the prepay, that could explain the lack of management. I believe everyone could be at your service, and it created problems. For example, I asked for sparkling water, but my glass was filled by still water for once.

This is the only restaurant where I could not get half of waiters' course introductions. It is true that they used lots of difficult plant names, but the distance they kept, volume and tone they speak were really the problem. There were hardly any eye contact. Course, lines, sauce, walk away.

The booking site suggested the 14-course to be a 2-3 hours meal. I have called the restaurant and was told they could definitely make it a 2 hours one, all I needed to do was notify my server. At the day of my reservation, server checked with the chief. He came persuading me to push my other appointment, which was not really possible but i do appreciate his professionalism. He told me 2 hours could be done, but I just had to eat really fast. Yes he denied that preparation required longer time, and offered to remind me when I eating pace fell behind. As a result I ate super fast, and ended up waiting longer than one usually would. Comparing with another table that came 15min earlier than we did, we were served under a normal pace, no rush at all. The last 3 dishes were all deserts, which were served all together by other fine restaurants. They made me wait 10 min for each of these bits. I ended up staying about 3 hours and still missed the last dish. I believe it was supposed to be a chocolate, and I waited 15 min for that it. 

I admit I should have make myself more available, but the servers attitude really pissed me off. After two hours, and with 3 courses left, I asked the server if they could speed it up. One male server, who had been slacking it off, suggested that I should just leave. Being offended by his answer, I stopped talking. He started pushing me to say "ok" so that they can stay with their current pace. One bond female server was well trained and keeps asking if I could give them more time so I could taste the rest of those dishes. The other dark hair female kept lying it usually took 3-4 hours and 2 hours was such an ask, but they were making those dishes faster and I should be GRATEFUL. She asked me how was the meal, I teasingly answered late. She started at me as if I said something ridiculous, then she repeatedly asked the question until my friend gave her an answer that satisfied her. Waited 15min for the last course, I stood up and asked for my coat. Nobody greeted me along the way. 

Initially I thought I would come back for the delicateness put on each dishes, but after 2 hours, I knew I would never come again.

Other cons: awkward height of the partition wall, one restroom.

Highly original and well executed, Aska deserves its 2 Michelin stars. It's a great addition to the Brooklyn restaurant scene offering something completely different than the usual high end tasting menus. Along with Chef's Table at Brooklyn Fare, Aska is making Brooklyn a destination for exciting, innovative, and refreshing restaurant experiences.

The food is seafood-centric, with surprisingly strong flavors helped along with concentrated broths and pickled accoutrements. Flavor experiences were augmented with a full palate of textures, such as the crispy dried seaweed with tiny dollops of puréed mussels, the grittiness of charred lamb heart mixed with creamy soothing sunchoke, and the gentle softness of the skate with celery root and celery root purée. Amazing.

The wine pairings were a highlight as well. Selections from Slovenia and Croatia mixed with French, Italian, and German wines made from varietals I've never heard of. There was a non-alcoholic milk as well!

Come here for innovation, beauty, and flavors. Come here for a wonderful time and a unique experience.

Best restaurant of 2016, 2 michelin stars... I had very high expectations and the food at Aska was kind of mind-blowing. I'd never had Scandinavian-style cuisine before, or rather "Modern Nordic grounded in Brooklyn" cuisine as the Chef sort of corrected me. It's very unique, even a little weird, and it's an amazing experience. 

The restaurant is minimalist, dim, almost unwelcoming, and it took me about 2 courses to start warming up to the spacious room. Mostly because of the staff. The staff were all fantastic, friendly and personal and not too formal. The chefs who work in the kitchen (every table has a great view) each come out to greet you and introduce every course. The Chef makes his rounds as well, and it's wonderful to listen to him talk about his food (listen hard, because he's very tall and softspoken). I was intimidated by the blood pancake - it's rich and almost chocolatey. Still quite strong for me, I didn't finish, but I'm glad I tried it. If you absolutely do not want it then you can request a plain pancake. A course of ash made from charred lamb heart... it sounds crazy but somehow it reminded me of bacon (VERY well-done bacon). Of course besides these, there were many many delicious not-so-crazy dishes. My favorite was lichen, fried and delicately crispy, over a lightly sweet caramelized cream, with an almost briny mushroom broth. Skate was presented on the bone with a luxuriously creamy celery root puree. The 120 day dry aged rib eye has my mouth watering even now. A dessert of fermented then pickled whole strawberries was the best strawberries I've ever had in the middle of winter, spooned over raw milk sorbet that was clean and refreshing.  

We were told the team actually forages for some ingredients, and these ingredients make quite an impression (mushrooms, moss, flowers). Most ingredients are transformed and used in interesting ways (as opposed to showcasing the simplicity of expensive ingredients). You have luxurious ingredients as well, but you get to appreciate more humble ingredients. Each dish has multiple components which are just okay on their own, but are great when eaten together. 

I believe this is one of the best values for set menus in New York, as the 19-course menu is $215 inclusive of tip. Highly recommend going for the extended tasting menu. They leave you with a printed menu and a beautifully crafted knife per diner, a little something to remind you of an incredible meal.

Just ate there. GREAT food. The service... ?? Our server, we opted on our table of four, for the wine pairing. Unfortunately, the pours were ridiculously small. 2 teaspoons?  Really? (We were later told that they "fill they up" after you drink the first taste, but they don't.) It spoiled most of the evening. For the money paid, they should err on the side of generosity.

Just came back from a trip in Iceland, so I was delighted to secure a reservation for this new Nordic restaurant that recently eared two michelin stars.   Prepay at reservation, gratuity and tax included.   Interesting system.  Sure makes a lot of things simpler.

I had high expectations for this restaurant, and Aska not only met it but was better.  Nineteen course meal too about 3 and half hours.   

Food is inventive and interesting.  The servers will tell you the ingredients, but it is likely that more than half of it's not something you've heard of before.  I'm not complaining as I take a lot of joy in trying new things.  Many courses will wow you, some will be just ok, but all are original and creative.  I was blown away by lamb's heart dish.  Burnt to ashes but it was lamb's heart nonetheless!

Ambiance is a huge factor here.  Black ceiling, black walls, black furnitures.  Staff dressed in black.  It seems really dark at first, but then again it's as if the chef wants you to focus your senses entirely on the food.  

My party of four were fortunate enough to get a table right next to the kitchen area, so we could observe some action from the sideline.  It was a pleasure to see everyone work in harmony, yet in complete silence most of the time.  It was amusing to see Chef Fredrik completely in focus, and he wasn't saying much but his presence was incredibly strong.  He may be a culinary genius.  I'm going to have to visit this place again to make sure.

After a positive experience at the previous Aska in Williamsburg, Chief Fredrik Berselius seems to have upped his game, greatly improving the setting and service, and more importantly improving on the menu.  Our meal reminded me of Noma in Copenhagen -  then the top rated restaurant in the world -- 18 months ago.  Heavy on Nordic flavors, berries, ferns, and other forest foliage, and of course fish.  Our ten courses were amazing,  This is a special meal and well worth the journey.  Also the prices of $145 per person is way below what one would pay for a similar quality meal in Manhattan.

Such an amazing dining experience!

We did the $145 tasting menu and it was one of the most creative meals I've had this year. Everything was delicious, well balanced and thoughtful; totally unique and unlike anything I had eaten this year. The service was great. They had heard we had dined at the old Aska, when it was still in kinfolk studios and every server we talked to wanted to know how we had liked our experience, etc. I can't wait to go back.

The original Aska closed in 2014 and reopened in 2016 to promptly become 2016's "top tasting menu restaurant in NYC." We started with cocktails on a rainy night as we waited for our private dining room to be ready. It was a very special birthday, and the ambience of the bar area was already a preview of the spectacular performance to come. 

Chef Frederik Berselius himself came out to greet us. He was charming and very direct in that Nordic manner. He approached my lactose intolerance with a bit of friendly Nordic chagrin, so I said it would be ok to include. (Really, he was very very nice about it, and I know that Chef wouldn't insist if he didn't think it was for the better. Much like my parents, right?) And yes, it is very difficult to eat Nordic cuisine when you can't have dairy. That and Italian. You know, in case you're planning to take me out to dinner.

The whole experience was beautiful, and the service impeccable. Creative, authentic, and very unique. Seafood-heavy, of course. The wine pairings were excellent, though for those who care, very heavy in whites (to accompany the seafood). The ambience transports you, and you forget you're in Brooklyn. There was a lot of discussion about possible after-dinner partying at Bembe, so save stomach space for sweaty Latin dancing. For those into that sort of thing. Which, I am. 

Unmissable, top notch experience.

Need more stars. Some friends and I did the 19-course (sic) tasting menu here, little private room in the book, for a bachelor party.

Fantastic.

The ceremony and sense-of-occasion was basically flawless; courses were presented with grace and detail (you WANT that, when you're dropping lots of bucks on a 4-hour meal); the wine pairings were treated with similar care.

The level of service extended to _deviations_ from the plan; I'd just come in from a flight and needed caffeine, and there was no sniffiness about working a coffee in between the best suited courses for timing, taste, etc. More substantively, they accommodated the fact that someone in our party (me) chooses not to eat all the meats offered on the tasting menu, and made smooth, tasty, and unfussy substitutions without impacting everyone else's experience.

And the food was grand. It was "fun" (cutting open bundles of spices wrapped around langoustines), varied in tone, and had lots of the kind of "earthy" deep flavors one might expect from Scandinavian foodie locavore-ish super-upmarket food of its kind. A couple of the deserts, in particular, stick in mind -- a kind of milk foam raw milk ice cream at the end with crunchy bits, especially. And that langoustine wrapped in herbs (not a desert).

This is obviously a (very) special occasion experience. But for something like that: it's absolutely grand, worth it, a treat.

Aska is a new two-star, tasting-menu-only Scandinavian-inspired restaurant in Brooklyn.
I was happy to find some available 'tickets' to buy - yes, tickets, as Aska is one of those places that has a theater-model of pricing. You simply buy and pay upfront during reservation, and then just show up.
I've been in all-but-two of two-star restaurants in NYC and can definitely say that this one met my expectations and is high up there in the ranking of the two-stars.
The tasting menu was a pleasure with only one or two dishes that I wasn't particularly fond of. My favourite dish would be the crab in crab soup as it was just so flavourful. You'll find a lot of Scandinavian touches here which will be familiar if you have experience with other high-end Scandinavian restaurants like Noma or Geranium in Copenhagen, for example the usage of ingredients like juniper or other needle trees.
Service was great, exactly what you would expect in a restaurant of this calibre, but just remember the ambiance, while dark, leans more towards business casual. You won't find waiters here dressed in suits like in some high-end French restaurants.
Fredrik was there and chatted with us for a good five minutes or more and told us his story of how he ended up here with this new redesigned Aska. I always like it when chefs go around and talk to each table towards the end of service.
Overall a great experience, I'll be back!

It was fun to experience but was expensive. Not sure if I'd come here again. Not exactly comfort food. Also location is way out in Williamsburg which is fun to trek to but again, you have to make it a special trip. Not a bad thing. Service was 5 star. Can't really beat it.

Can't describe this experience in a few words, but I will try.. 

My boyfriend took me here on my birthday last week. We're greeted by a warm ambiance and friendly hosts. We ordered a few drinks and were seated immediately. The kitchen is completely open and we see the head chef working diligently. The open kitchen was a plus - it's really nice to see the chefs working on your food as they come out. 

We ordered the 10 course meal which took slightly north of 3 hours. Very happily full by then. The servers were very accommodating and each entree was served by the chefs who were making it. The head chef came by our table a few times to talk to us - he was incredibly friendly and even more skilled. 

We will definitely be back to try to 17 course meal. The best entree was the 120 day dry aged steak or the moss dish - slightly fried with a mushroom broth. Simply delicious.

First time tried Scandinavian food, and chef Fredrik Berselius did impress us. We did the 19 course tasting menu, the full experience took around 4 hours.

The moment I stepped into the restaurant, I knew I'm gonna love this place. From interior decorations to food presentation and flavor, everything has a sense of minimalistic aesthetic. They use novel ingredients to present the originality of the flavor, and also have some bold experiments with the food such as the blood pancake. The tasting menu started with fresh blue mussels, just the right way to arouse my appetite. My favorite dishes of the night was the langoustine, which was cooked in aromatic herbs and was really tender and juicy. My friend an I also enjoyed the Maine oyster and the caviar. 

Scandinavian food stresses clean flavor and fresh ingredients, so I guess it probably won't please someone who likes heavy or creamy taste cuisine. The service was top notch as well. Overall, the dinning experience was incredible and I highly recommend it for a romantic date night.

One of our favorite foodie experiences in NY was at WD50 years ago. Over the years, we've eaten at renowned restaurants in NY, but nothing has come close since. Except now at Aska.

We did the 10 course tasting menu with drinks pairing (we were full at the end of the evening, I think the 19 course would have been too much food for us). We sat at the table facing the kitchen, it was fascinating watching them spending so much time perfecting each dish before it came out - and each was like a piece of art. The meticulousness and level of detail was quite amazing. Apart from the visual aesthetics, the food is interesting too - makes you think eating things you would have never thought of before. And of course delicious. 

We were informed when we arrived that we had the table for the whole evening. It's certainly nice not to be rushed at all, to have the luxury of time, to relax, chat, and enjoy the experience.

The staff there are warm, friendly, helpful, which made Aska extra special (isn't very annoying when you have to deal with rude obnoxious waitstaff, why do certain restaurants have that culture?). They accommodated our food restrictions, we had informed them via the site in advance. They double-checked with us about a couple of things when we arrived.

The bartender downstairs makes excellent cocktails. She's also very warm and chatted with us for a while, she even made a couple of special cocktails based on what we had said we liked.

All in all, a very happy evening. I want to go again and next time try out their back garden.

This restaurant is completely restored my faith in high-end meals in NYC. 

I'm sure one can dissect each course in detail in the other reviews, but all I will say is the tastes you will experience here are somehow both unbelievably delicious, and so novel they feel as if they are out of a dream.  Imagine taking the amazingness of toast and putting it in the form of a soup... or taking the woodsy flavor of mushrooms and maple syrup and assembling it into ice cream......or combining a chinese plum with chocolate and serving it on a small twig ...these all happen at Aska.

In comparison to a recent excursion to another newcomer to the NYC restaurant scene, Gunter Seeger, another  michelin winner of this past year (albeit single star), Aska is so much better I feel the money I spent at Gunter Seeger might as well have been flushed down the drain. Sometimes, at these more conventional "fancy" places it seems as if you pay ridiculous amounts for tiny, pretentious courses with random assortments of ingredients blended, liquified, and dabbed on a plate. Aska could not be further from this. This restaurant is what I  thought these kind of restaurants could be. The preparations are not only purposeful, but so surprisingly interesting I have no idea how anyone could have thought them up.

Aska is worthy of all of it's recent accolades.

Of course, service and setting, etc is great too, if you care about this sort of thing.
Amazing experience. Every dish was explosion of tastes. Perfectly planed menu. Can't wait to go again and tell all my friends to take this experience. Best in New York!

Delectable. Gorgeous. Shakespearean. Pastoral. Unexpected. Titillating. Norwegian Punk. Savoury. Sexy. Black Box Theater. Caviar. Lichen. Silky wine. Ibsen. Misty garden. Blue mussels. Cured skate. Lilac. Birchwood. Milk sorbet. Grilled onion. Locally sourced. Farms at twilight. Preserved pine. Blood pancake. Sparkling. Glimmering. Shimmering. Generous.  Unforgettable. Midsummer dreams. Exotic cream. Brilliant. Artful. Flowering dill. Spring woods. Mushroom broth. Pork butter. Experimental. Showering during a thunderstorm.

Go.

I can not quite call this a meal, as it was more of an exploratory and sensory experience. The combination of ingredients and presentation was a delight to all of my senses. The food looked and tasted amazing. Each bite varied a bit, depending on what parts of the dish were scooped up into the fork or spoon. Some dishes felt like they were taken straight from the cuisine of some mythical land where dragons roam the earth (lamb heart). Others looked and tasted like they were brought forth from an enchanted forest (lichen). Overall, this was a superb experience.

WONDERFUL place.  The food, of course goes without saying is excellent.  But the experience is what makes it.  The people are just so nice.  Such personal attention and care.  Not pretentious at all (like Blue Hill at Stone Barn for example).  The price is also quite justifiable for a 2 Michelin Star right out of the gate (doesn't Blue Hill only have one, just saying) that INCLUDED service.  No tipping allowed!  Gotta love Europeans.  They truly want you to have an experience here and not just take your money.  It was affordable even WITH a bottle of wine.  Normally, places like this I don't even look at the "by the bottle" list, because it's usually not reasonable (like Blue Hill...I don't like them, if you could not tell).  

Because we did not do the pairing, we decided to do a bottle, and asked for a suggestion as to which would go best with most of the courses.  She (so lovely) suggested white and asked what we normally like, then believed she had something perfect although thought they might be out.  It actually wasn't on the menu, and turns out the did still have one bottle left.  She brings it out for us to try, and we LOVED it!  It was absolutely perfect, she is brilliant.  Now, remember, it's not on the menu, sooooo of course we were a little nervous.  Normally a place would suggest/bring you the most expensive bottle given the opportunity (like Blue Hill, again, OK I'll stop now).  To our very pleasant surprise, it was probably one of their cheapest bottles!  Did I mention how much I love Europeans?  My only wish is that there was maybe one more course, that would have been perfect, I was still a little hungry and remember thinking to myself: "I could use one more"...

Since we just loved the place so much after our dining experience, and the people there are so kind, we decided to check out the bar/outdoor garden out back one Friday eventing.  Again, such great people, and the casual snacks were so simple, but so delicious.  Even something so simple as bread, theirs was literally the best bread I have ever had in my life.

Born and trained in Sweden, his creativity previously on display at Frej and Aska at Kinfolk Studios before aska moved beneath the Williamsburg bridge and earned Two Michelin Stars, Fredrik Berselius has continued to defy New York's fine dining conventions of luxury ingredients and jackets-required dining rooms, the come-as-you are feel and willingness to take chances certainly not for the timid, but quite impressive for those willing to place their trust in the kitchen. 

Unmarked at its location on South 5th Street, the outside grey with black doors while the interior is an austere combination of brick, wood and spotlights, entrance to aska is followed by a smiling welcome from a hostess followed by the restaurant's GM, the use of Tock for pre-payment ensuring the room to be filled each day for a 19-course menu with the diner's proclivities dictating the meal's pace.

High ceilinged and hard, unseen speakers floating a mellow soundtrack above the room, it was just past six o'clock that Chef Berselius greeted the first wave of patrons, he and his team clearly having done their research as he inquired about where people were from, what they liked and why they had decided to visit his restaurant.

Offering a list of Wines by the Glass and Cocktails from the downstairs Bar, a 2013 Harslevalu going very well with approximately 3/4 of the menu, dinner began with a crisp Leaf of Bladderwrack with Blue Mussel Cream followed by a sizable Bread board and two spreads, the Sourdough Loaf and Barley Mash Roll both excellent, as was the Lardo-reminiscent whipped Pork Fat.

Going strong from the start and rarely letting up, an ebb and flow of finger foods and one-to-two bite morsels, the second course placed a plump Langoustine at the center of a bundle of Chamomile kissed by a blowtorch and snipped open diners, the smoky sweetness countered by Nasturtium, while the follow-ups featured a Potato puff topped in smoked Fish Roe and trimmed Oysters next to sour Gooseberries with a gentle hint of Pine.

Presenting the next plate as a single bite described as 'Sourdough and Hake,' the flavor rich and smoky with the crispy Milk Skin adding a textual element, the next two courses continued the charred theme by way of un-cured Sturgeon Roe straight from a Finnish Farm bathed in roasted Onions followed by a dollop of Lamb fat and pureed Sunchoke covered in Ash, the fact that those ashes came from a Lamb Heart completely imperceptible as the flavor was almost exclusively bitter save for a mild acidic note. 

Bringing in live Scallops and merely kissing them with flame before opening the shell at course eight, the light florals of Elderflower building toward Berselius' famous Blood Pancake topped in Roses and Rosehips to follow, dinner crossed the mid-point with a quenelle of Norwegian King Crab served in an aromatic broth ready to be fortified with Egg Yolk, the 'burnt' Potatoes a little tough but a pleasant contrast to the Crustacean's briny sweetness.

Doing an admirable job of linking and transitioning flavors throughout the meal, but quickly pressing the 'reset' button by way of a crisp slice of Kohlrabi on ice before progressing to the evening's final four savories, aska's Skate was unfortunately compromised by several small bones despite the small portion, the "Lichen" a far better dish that was light in weight but rich in umami with a bright finish thanks to the Spruce Vinegar.

Serving a slimy Squid Tart as the penultimate savory, the combination of salt, smoke and fresh Horseradish not particularly delicious on its own but tying in nicely to the dry-aged Beef and intensely acidic sauce to follow, desserts took the predictable route of two Ice Creams followed by Mignardises, the "Lilac" properly described by the presenting Chef as a "mouthful of Flowers" while the follow-up was as delicious as it was bizarre, the Ice Cream essentially just a satin canvas for the candied and raw mushrooms plus sweet Woodruff.
great restaurant in Brooklyn. worth a try..kinda of creamy. but the fish, steak beef, oysters and also caviar are the best

Amazing Williamsburg location,, fine dining at its best. This jacket required dress code is enforced and you are well attended to! Will definitely come back. Well worth the money and well deserving of a 2 Michelin Star!
Sorry about okd review posted by accident. Food was very good . insightful Scandinavian flavors done really well. Chef was very nice, too. would definitley return!

Seen the comment,we decided to give a try today for my birthday,after 30 mins drove there did not see this restaurant at 47 S5st,only 57 there is a bar which was told another name,I called the number twice did not get thru.what's going on?did they change address?

The staff at Aska clearly put a great deal of effort and energy into creating interesting food at the top level of dining experiences in NY.  The staff were welcoming and friendly. I loved the non-alcoholic drinks pairing of creative and tasty juice combinations!  That all being said, my husband and I felt that 19 super-rich courses were way too much and left us feeling ill at the end, and not in a good way. We like high-end dining, but this was over the top and unfortunately it really detracted from the overall experience. Maybe five fewer courses or interspersing it with less rich fare and it would have been just right.

Excellent. We started with great cocktails in the backyard and then moved into the dining room. Had the 19 course which - with bread - left us pretty stuffed. But the dishes were all delicious and/or inventive. Many seafood based. A couple heart-based. Perhaps the best meal I've had in New York.

Lots of hits and misses but overall and amazing dining experience and I highly recommend this restaurant, especially those that are trying to explore haute nordic cuisine. Somehow, with very limited training, the head chef was able to create this (seriously funded) restaurant in Brooklyn with such success so early on. Plating and service is impeccable. Ambiance, including outdoor garden/waiting room, is great. They use "local" ingredients that they either plant themselves or hunt for in the immediate area. Gluten-free bread starter made of sunflower flour still haunts my fantasies. Langoustine in herb bundle was beautiful but flavors didn't quite work.120-day dry aged rib eye was excellent but would have done better without the odd black currant sauce. Smoked scallop was a huge winner. Onion and caviar dish was a bit confused. Birchwood ice cream was unique and I enjoyed it more than my friend.

We were there in early September for our anniversary. The setup of this place is essentially a show with taste of the food prepared by the actors.  The seating area is very dark and the kitchen is bright and surrounded by all the dinning tables.

Food were absolutely beautiful. Each is a piece of art. Taste of the food were in general very good however they were not as impressive as the presentation of the food. What really lacked was the smell of the food. Only a handful of dishes out of our 19 course tasting were giving my pleasure from the aroma of the ingredients. 

The service was friendly and patient and yet not pretending. All staff in this place were young. I'd guess their average age is about 27. And it seemed they didn't have particular division of responsibilities such that the person who was preparing my food sometimes also served it. And that included the young head chef himself. 

In general we enjoyed the unique experience very much.
We have been here twice. The chef is awesome as he picks up ingredients from the nature and really puts thoughts into the cuisine.  Hope everyone could give him a try. He is really cool.

It's a cute restaurant right next to Miss Favela, a fun little Brazilian bar. We got the 19 course menu. Almost everything was pretty good. The food here is definitely better than the food at the previous Aska place.

Aska provides the full experience--beautiful meal, thoughtful service

My husband and I chose the 19-course meal for our first dinner in NYC, and Aska did not disappoint. The bites were beautiful, inventive, seasonal, and poetic. It is obvious the care with which Chef Fredrik and his team take to create and plate each dish. The items are familiar enough to feel comfortable, yet unique enough to provide an unforgettable culinary experience (moss? heart ash? birch and mushroom ice cream? All sound crazy but they were delicious.). Each course is designed to highlight the beauty of the ingredient and usually offers the ingredient in multiple ways. I don't usually prefer oysters, but these oysters were amazing, nor do I like mushrooms, yet they were delicious in the ice cream. (I couldn't even imagine the dessert when I read about it online, but seriously, it was awesome.)

GET THE JUICE PAIRING!! I opted for the juice pairing (+ a couple of glasses of wine...I just can't handle all the courses of a wine pairing haha). The juice pairing was one of the highlights of the meal!!! The juices were so inventive and truly accompanied/enhanced each course. My husband is very much a "wine guy," and a week late he still wishes he'd gotten the juices instead! 

The service at Aska was truly impeccable. I hate to use that word and sound pretentious, but I don't know what else to say--they were incredible! Our server was professional, sweet, and knowledgeable. The sommelier and juice maker knew the food and pairings perfectly. Each member of the kitchen staff presented his dish to us and explained it, answering any questions we had about preparation or sources. No one, however, was stuffy or too formal. They all joked and chatted like friends as the night wore on...we were there for almost 4 1/2 hours! 

We chose to finish our dessert courses outside in the courtyard, and it was so intimate and cozy. Lights were strung over the courtyard, and they had warm blankets to wrap up in. As we were some of the last guests to leave, Chef Fredrik and some of the team even joined us outside to chat and take photos. 

Our entire Aska experience was truly a pleasure.

Sublime.   Food.  Service. Pacing between courses.  Wine pairing.   Attention to detail. Design of the space, particularly distance between the diners, created a feeling that you were at home with your own private collection of chefs. Perfect for a special evening.

When I think of Scandinavian decor, I typically think of light, white, and airy spaces. Not Aska. When you enter through the velvet curtains, you just see black, black, and more black - but the kitchen is starkly lit up with pendant lamps, the chefs given centerstage while us diners sit in the shadows and watch them work their magic.

I had the 19-course, $250 menu (price includes service but excludes tax) and almost every dish was stellar. If you enjoy seafood and cured fish products (think trout and caviar), you'll love Aska. Only one of the 19 dishes was a land meat dish - and the 120 day dry-aged beef cut like butter.

Several dishes came with a broth or a sauce that's served tableside, all of them punchy with flavor. I was constantly delighted by the next dish and the next - and it's hard to do that with 19 courses. My favorites were probably the crispy lichen, squid tart, scallop with elderberry and elderflower, and the langoustine cooked in lavender (that you had to snip off with a nose hair trimmer). The birchwood ice cream topped with a variety of candied and raw mushrooms was also amazing - I love it when non-traditionally dessert foods like vegetables are made into desserts, and the earthiness of the mushrooms just worked so well.

I unfortunately did NOT like the blood pancake at all. I'm not a stranger to congealed blood, having eaten that growing up in Southeast Asia, but something about the mushy, cakey texture AND the iron taste just wasn't very appetizing.

Service was excellent, and dishes came out well-paced despite it being a full Saturday night. I would certainly come back here again to see what delights might await me during the spring/summer seasons.

I booked this place for my husband's birthday. There were no weekend reservations available so I took a weekday. I noted on their reservation website that it was for a birthday and any food restrictions and preferences. When we arrived, they said they did not get my notes but noted that it was a birthday.

When you walk into the place, it is super dark, but then you see streams of light coming from all around, There are not many tables in the restaurant which tells me it will be quite the experience for every party of diners that walk through the door.

There is a beautiful outside garden that is decorated with latern lights. There is also a small back room that can seat I believe 6-8 for a private party? 

They have an open kitchen concept so you see everything that the chef's are working on. 

As we walk in, we are greeted but not just 1 person, but everyone on the team which was very nice. We got seated at a corner table by the window which I loved and had a great view of the open kitchen. I cannot say enough good things about the service and the experience we had here. 

I had booked the juice pairing for my husband (just for him) and the juices were a pleasant surprise and also very unique. it ranged from a rose soda, the an apple lemon juice, to a pair juice, to a green juice, etc. 
The food came out in a very timely manner. Each dish was introduced by a different chef who actually served each dish to you.

You have to either love Scandinavian cuisine or you have to be extremely open minded to all new foods. Most of the items I loved and was surprised by. Other items I felt was a bit strange for my taste and didn't understand too much. The langoustine and caviar were delicious.The beef and fish dish were out of this world, paired with the most delicious sauce that made you want to lick it off the plate. 
There was a plate in between, a pig blood pancake with a marinated flower combo... this was strange as the the flowers on top were sour. Sour to a point my face cringed. I was shocked since so many dishes before it were so good!   
There were 2 desserts that were served to us. One was amazing, a ice cream served with a strawberry soup. It was delightful and fresh, a perfect way to end the meal. The second dessert confused me a bit as it was a powder type of ice cream sitting in a pool of syrup with raw mushrooms on top. 
The birthday aspect was missed as after dessert was served, the server brought out a candle and placed it on the table... I appreciated the after thought but knew it was forgotten. 

Overall, I would rate the food pretty good; a good experience but I would rate the service 2 thumbs up!

I came for my birthday dinner and we had a 19-course tasting menu with the wine pairing.  I'd like to think we're adventurous and relatively well-eaten* and even with our food vocabulary, we were still surprised by several of the dishes.

Example 1: the bread comes with a cultured butter and then another white dish filled with what the Hubs said tasted like "meat soup".  Turns out it's whipped pig fat.  Whoa.  Both delicious and disgusting. I'll eat that all day.
Example 2: Langoustine dish that came with nail scissors to open the lavender satchel with. I don't know how those little guys were cooked (or not cooked) but they were delicious, plump, succulent, and beautifully floral.  Nice job.
Example 3: Lamb heart.  But turned into powder.  If they had profered a metal straw, you could've snorted it.  Super weird but powerfully flavorful (in the mouth, not through the nose).

Let's just say all the food is delicious and you should try it.  

Service here is amazing.  The hostesses all wear very scandinavian tunics and up-dos but exude the warmth of a thousand mugs of hot chocolate (with marshmallows).  They patiently answer any question no matter how stupid and will hang around and chat with you about wine if you so desire.  They also magically take plates and glasses away like culinary ninjas.  The hoard of cooks in the kitchen is a perfectly timed dance troupe.  They bring out these beautifully plated dishes and explain the sometimes quite exotic ingredients and it's more like a show than a meal.

The best part is that when you make the hard-to-get reservations, you get the table for the whole night.  No one awkwardly hovering over you trying to get your table turned over to squeeze in more people.

Totally deserving of those 2 Michelin stars.

Thanks Hubs!   


-------
* a version of "well-read", I'd like to think.

This was one of the best birthday dinners I've ever had... If you're looking to wine and dine someone very special, this is definitely the place to take them!! I rank this higher than many of the "World's Best Restaurants."

19 course tasting menu + juice pairing + select cocktails = 4 hours of bliss.

[FOOD]
I won't go through each and every dish, but there were definitely some VERY notable dishes that I still remember clear as day as I write this review 5 months after.

The ingredients they used in every dish were so unique and out of this world. All harvested from places like... a tree under the Williamsburg Bridge, or oysters from a random New England island caught earlier that day, or quite literally from their own garden in the backyard.  There were quite a lot of ingredients that I did not recognize.

*Bread & Butter - the cultured fat was amazing
*Langoustine Pommes Souffle
*Oyster
*Milk Skin
*Scallop
*King Crab
*Kohlrabi (compressed linden leaf)
*Squid Tart

One particular dish stands out to me so vividly, and that's the Lamb Heart.  You are quite literally eating ashes of lamb hearts.  The flavor was SO strong, I don't think I'll ever forget it.  It tastes exactly as you would think ashes of lamb hearts would taste like.  It wasn't for me, but I recommend everyone trying it at least once.

Presentation of each and every dish was done w/ such delicacy and precision. 

[ATMOSPHERE]
There are only about 10 tables in the entire restaurant, all spaced out with a good distance from each other.  All have view of the open kitchen as you watch these chefs do their magic and plate your beautiful dishes.  It is quite romantic. You can stay for the remainder of the night because they only take so many reservations.  We were able to move to the garden area to have our dessert course in private.  It was beautiful out there... Honestly, it's not a bad place to plan a proposal!!

[SERVICE]
Impeccable. Chefs came over to the table to present each dish, their origin, the ingredients, the pairings... I felt so well informed.

[JUICE PAIRING] 
Expensive? Yes. Who knew you could charge so much for juice? But honestly, it was really good. Some of the juices were just SO good.  I'm still trying to figure out how something so simple could taste so good.  I'm not sure how they made their apple and beet juice but it was the best I've ever had.

[BOTTOM LINE]
Take someone who deserves only the best.

Aska - what might you think is this? Read on the find out.

Maine seaweed with blue mussel emulsion is a bowl of near buttery sea water.

The langostino torched with langostino head broth and nasturtiums is nearly effervescent. Silky and rich, the taste of shrimp/lobster in its own broth creates an deep, rich flavor.

A Wiley point oyster from Maine, poached at 62 degrees in a cream emulsion of ora pine and oyster emulsion combines the forest and the sea in one perfect bite.

Hake milk bun brings in an Asian take on a Scandinavian favorite but sandwiching flaky bake in a sought bite.

Sturgeon caviar and onions softly caramelized in a broth of creme fresh make spending $2000 on a tin of fish eggs seem nearly plausible.

A dish of pulverized smoked lamb hearts with Jerusalem artichoke consists of a fine powder of lamb essence sprinkled over Jerusalem artichokes as a cream.

A seared scallop in Elderberry broth is lightly poached and exquisitely translucent, creamy. 

A slight hiccup in service as the hot broth was spilled on both arms here - almost certainly not accidental - this incident was a minor blip in the overall meal.

Pigs ear blood pancake with pickled flowers, elderberry jam and beets nearly recreates a spring afternoon with snow still melting. The intense flavor of pancake sweeetened slightly by elderberry and earth beets.

Kolrabi with lichen vinaigrette is a palate cleanser, the vinaigrette is almost a broth in the approximation of cole slaw.

The Skate wing skate in a reduction of celery root and dill vinaigrette combines the silken feel of puréed celery root with dill. Served on the bone, the fish is subtle and buttery.

Lichen with mushroom broth arrives deep fried. Eating lichen as a dish had never been contemplated until
This moment but with its forest neighbor as flavor enhancer, the crisp moss sops up the earthy mushroom essence.

The 120 day dry aged rib eye with chopped fat cap and elderberry, salted lightly is pure indulgence and extraordinary. Ordering this for one would be sublime / the luscious fat melting into the smooth, rich meat. 

For dessert, Raw milk sorbet with strawberry and fermented starberry juices is tart, sweet and settling.

The Birchwood ice cream with shaved mushrooms again defies expectations and brings unexpected items together onto a plate.

House made Chocolates to finish.

Those are the dishes served the evening we spent 4 hours at asks. The earth, sea, air and forest permeated every dish. The service is great. The food spectacular. The setting and attention to detail can be mind numbing. The drink pairing worth adding.

Good fine dining place! Somehow i find the dishes were a bit heavy in texture and form. I didnt feel light and energetic at the end of the tasting menu but rather heavy and sluggish. But it was good to try at least once since there are not that many two Michelin star restaurants in new york anyway.
Anazing small plates in the downstairs bar! Suh a sweet hidden spot, the plates are super subtiles and delicious, and and and the place is calm too which is just so refreshing!
We had a tasting 10 course menu. Nope. Go to Gabriel Kreurher if U want to enjoy the food and the art of cooking.

HOLY MOLY. This was such a special experience. If you are really into food and want to celebrate an occasion, come here. Seriously. It is absolutely worth the money. 

We sat for the extended tasting (I think it wound up being 16 courses) but there are several options to choose from. We also opted to do the wine pairing for $175 per person (they topped us off a few times too). After doing some research we found the wines were on average ~$40ish per bottle, which I'm impressed by. It shushes the "money=quality" wine stereotype. 

Before dinner we had cocktails, which were absolutely outstanding. I recommend going early to do the same. I had a Wild negroni. 

The hospitality and service here were great. Everyone knew it was my boyfriend's birthday! And the staff asked us about where we were from, etc. and seemed like they were genuinely interested in talking with us. They even gave us pizza recommendations in the area. 

The chef came by at the end of the dinner which I really appreciated. 

All around, Aska is a warm, wholesome, and enriching yet impressive experience that also teachesa lot about food and flavor. There were so many highlights of the meal that I know we will be talking about forever.

Fantastic overall. Compared to other Michelin star restaurants the menu could be better. Everything on it however, tasted great, just needed a heartier selection. The service was top top top notch. Our server Rachel was knowledgeable and enthusiastic. We had a great time and again, the service was the best. Definitely go there for the service and atmosphere. Worthy of its stars.

There's a reason this is a Michelin two star restaurant (although I believe it deserves a 3rd), it's exceptional.

The food is truly exquisite, the atmosphere calming, and most importantly, the staff is warm and welcoming. Our sommelier was especially knowledgeable, sharing more offbeat discoveries that paired perfectly with each plate. Everything from the food to the service was executed to perfection. A delightful pleasure indeed. 

I can't wait to come back this summer to experience the outdoor garden!
This was my first tasting menu... Every dish was so carefully put together. I tasted flavors that I've never dreamed of! The staff and atmosphere really made it a memorable experience. Worth it.

Wow. Simply wow. 

Having traveled to the Scandinavian counties countless of times, I fell in love with the cuisine. The simplicity of the flavors yet complexity of combining these natural ingredients together is breathtaking. It's very farm to table and all the ingredients couldn't be any more fresh. 

I wanted to take my boyfriend here for his birthday since he never tried Scandinavian food before. I didn't think there would be decent Scandinavian food in New York but boy was I proven wrong. 

ASKA deserves all two of its Michelin stars.. I would even argue it deserves three. From the service to the atmosphere and the food, it SCREAMS THREE MICHELIN STARS. 

We did the 19 course menu and got a bottle of wine to share as well as the elderflower tea and the wild negroni. 

Let's start with the service. We came in somewhat wet from the rain and was greeted warmly by the staff as they quickly warmed us up through friendly conversation. 

I could already tell it was going to be a great night. 


We were quickly brought to our table and I was given a little stool for my bag! Honestly, what other restaurant would think of this? Something this simple yet super thoughtful was very appreciative. Thank you! 

I can't even go into detail about the food because there's literally no way to describe it. You need to come here and experience everything yourself!

I took my wife here for her birthday, treating her to the 19 course dinner with wine pairing. It was a truly memorable, unique experience.

Housed in a square black room, with an open kitchen taking up one corner, the restaurant also has an outdoor garden and a downstairs white-brick bar and lounge, as there is no bar in the dining room.

The black dining area offers an almost liturgic experience; there are a few, well spaced round table, and the overall feel is dark and intimate, with spotlights illuminating the busy open kitchen. In fact, I think I counted 8 or 9 chefs working in the kitchen at any given time that evening, and it was the chefs who actually brought each dish to our table and then described it to us. I liked that a lot, as through the evening we got to know all the chefs. You also eat at your own pace: you have the table for the evening, so you can take your time to savor this sensory experience in full.

The 19 course menu was incredibly eclectic and inventive, with amazing attention to details. The last time I've experienced something this dazzling was at WD-50. Consider something as simple as the bread basket, which not only comes with 3 different types of bread, but with 2 different types of butter too: a brown butter and another one made with whipped pig fat.

I'm not going to mention all the 19 courses we had[1], but a few of them stood out for various reasons. Such as:
- Lamb Heart, which is a cured lamb heart burnt in bedstraw, pulverized, and then served as a powder with pickled sunchoke.
-Scallop, which is served with its own roe, elderberry and elderflower.
- The Langoustine is cooked in a lavender and nasturtium satchel, and comes with small scissors to open the satchel, almost like a present.
- The Squid Tart is made with seaweed, charred squid, and a puree made from dulse.
- Lichen, served with reduced and caramelized cream, preserved pine shoots, broth from chanterelle mushrooms, and spruce vinegar.
-Ice cream made from Birchwood with black trumpet, pine mushrooms, and woodruff.

The wine pairing was equally full of excellent wines and a couple of surprises including two amazing Hungarian wines: a Somlói Vándor's Juhfark, and a Furmint & Hárslevelü Kardoz Tokaj.

The bill is not for the faint of heart, and one has to pay in advance at the time of reservation, but I feel it was totally worth it. A unique experience we will remember for a very long time.
--------------------
[1] You can checkout the pictures I took, as they cover all dishes we had. Just keep in mind that the menu changes often.

Two michelin stars.
Innovative cuisine.
Quiet, welcoming space.

We tried the abbreviated menu ($185) of 10 dishes, which means a two-hour dining experience.

Most dishes were excellent, with the kudos going to the meat dish and lichen dish, and maybe a couple of disappointments, esp. the radish dish.

As Insaid -- One exceptional dish was the lichen in brooth. Incredible.

Overall you will taste new flavors and textures, be surprised, and be well taken care of.

I think main disappointment was the wine list, a tad expensive, and missing a couple of more classic options (Bordeaux for sure, some white Burgundy's like Chassagne-Montrachet or Corton-Charlemagne, or more well-known Champagne).

Went here for Anniversary dinner. Overall the atmosphere is good. Minimalist and Scandinavian style. Food idea is very creative with local ingredients, vegan in nature. All herbs grown in house. Tried the juice pairing and like the concept.

I came here with my friend on her birthday.  Personally I don't like a restaurant is dark, it really depend who you come with.  The portion of food is small, I end up ordered 2 different dishes.  For 2 person, about $100.  uh.. little expensive.  But it is okay for birthday girl haha.

The restaurant is really good, but it rubbed me the wrong way that two of the courses were bread with either butter or olive oil. I get it, it was very sophisticated butter, but still.. I felt like it took away from the experience. We also didn't have the meat dish that multiple Yelp reviewers mentioned and when we asked why, they told us it was because we had chosen the long menu and it was only offered on the shorter version. I wish I had known that prior to pre-paying the dinner. Overall it was okay... it might be that my palate isn't sophisticated enough, but I didn't see (or taste) what the huge fuzz was about.

Went here for my boyfriend's birthday for the abbreviated tasting menu. 

I had MAJOR subway delays and got to the restaurant a half an hour after our reservation - I found my bf enjoying a cocktail in their beautiful garden, and when I got there, they didn't rush me at all. In fact, they let us know we could take our time outside and just let them know when we wanted to come in and get started, which I thought was so nice and pretty rare. 

Every single thing we tasted was phenomenal. I am a vegetarian, and they were able to accommodate a separate vegetarian tasting menu for me (while my bf was able to enjoy the regular tasting). Each dish was unique, with purposeful elements and surprising flavors. We thoroughly enjoyed our entire meal here. The wines we tasted were phenomenal - I only wish they had a few more affordable options. 

All in all, this is a great place for a special meal. Definitely an NYC must-eat.

Run by Swedish chef Fredrik Berselius this two Michelin star Brooklyn restaurant is a hidden gem. Such pure tastes served in a stellar space. Everything about this place is perfect. From the lovely outdoor garden to the downstairs cellar bar, the dimly lit tones added to the amazing ambience. Stays true to it's Nordic roots! A must try.

Love this place, the chef was in the house and he was readily available and very involved with everything. The meals tasted delicious and are like edible art pieces! So fun to eat, very memorable. I took my husband for his birthday and he loved it : ) The staff overall is excellent, I really enjoyed my time here.

Delicious, interesting, and just overall a special experience. The downstairs lounge is super comfortable and they have a garden area. We had the full tasting and it was delightful and tasty. Great for a special occasion.

The somm was also great and on point with her recommendations for us. Her wine suggestions really elevated our dinner.

This was a fun and tasty tasting menu. We paired it with the wine pairing. The place has a nice patio. We started with the appetizer course on the patio, and then moved indoors for the main courses. It was a lovely evening so we requested to be on the patio for dessert course. The meal is long; ours took 4.5 hours. Overall excellent meal. Worth the price tag.

My bf and I arrived a little early for our reservation, so we were offered to relax at the bar downstairs. There was only one other couple downstairs, it was very intimate and cozy. The cocktail was obviously great, syrupy and smooth. We were called upstairs to our table before we finished our drinks. For the night, we opted for the full dinner menu and a drink pairing. The food was good but not as light and fresh as I was expecting for a summer visit to a Scandinavian restaurant. I thought a number of their dishes had very heavy oils that turned my stomach a bit. I am still giving them 4 stars because my bf did not agree and so this might have been a preference issue. There were some true gems offered with the drink pairing, but I have learned a lesson. I drink far more than beverage pairings offer. The waiter gave us a few "free" pours just because we had finished the drinks before the food got there. We never have the intention of getting drunk, but I always find myself straining to stretch those few teaspoons of fine wine. Finally, I begrudge myself for saying this, but the waitstaff was awkward. He attempted multiple times to have a conversation with us, which was fine, but his comments felt extremely perfunctory and structured. With the stringent beverage pours and the awkward staff, we felt the place was too stuffy to warrant a return for now. But I will still give 4 stars because the food and wine was A level, not stars because experience overall was less than desired.

Fantastic evening. Creative and exceptional flavors. The chef is an artist with the food. The service staff is low key and extremely professional and friendly..no snooty or highbrow atmosphere here. My better half and I have dined at all the top rated NYC restaurants over the past 10 years including all of the Michelin starred venues and this was right up there with them regarding the food, ambiance and service. The chef/owner is also very friendly and approachable if you have a question as were all of his other chefs working with him that night. We will return.

I had dinner at Aska with my mom and my cousin last month, during a gluttonous trip to New York. It was an extraordinary experience, with immaculate service and wonderful food. I ate several things here that were completely new to me, even familiar ingredients presented in surprising ways.

We reserved a table for three a couple of weeks in advance. Aska requires payment for food at time of booking, a system I've only ever seen from super fancy restaurants, where a dinner reservation is like a ticket to a show. We opted for the abbreviated tasting--about ten courses for $185, as opposed to $265 for 16 to 18--and chose the earlier seating, at 6:00. When it turned out my cousin couldn't leave work that earlier, we were able to move our reservation to 7:30 over the phone.

My mom and I arrived first, and we waited for my cousin on the lovely, peaceful patio. We moved inside for dinner, to the stylish dining room, where our table was set with crisp black tablecloth, soothing candle, and tiny potted plant. There was an open kitchen, where we could watch the busy cooks putting together all those complicated dishes. Service was outstanding. Our server Morgan was the consummate host, guiding us through this elaborate dinner with warmth and absolute competence.

We started our night with cocktails. I got the Wild Negroni, a perfumed negroni with chrysanthemum gin, Salers Aperitif, and Cocchi Americano. My cousin had the Teak, a dry and pleasantly medicinal mix of Amontillado sherry, dry and blanc vermouth, and aquavit, served in a teak cup. The three of us then shared a wine pairing with our meal, and this was fun and well conceived, with something like six wines, mostly whites, to go with our food.

The first two courses were bite-sized snacks, paired with a pour of Riesling. Crispy twigs of dried bladderwrack seaweed came dotted with blue mussel emulsion over a bed of kelp and rocks (we were instructed not to eat the kelp, which us Koreans definitely would've eaten otherwise). Then, beautiful half-moon wedges of kohlrabi, marinated and compressed with linden leaf oil and linden flower vinegar, finished with radish flowers and cucumber powder. I can't really describe the flavor or texture of this exquisite bite--it was unlike anything I'd ever had before. After this, we had our first bread service: fresh manitoba bread made with buttermilk and IPA, dotted with sunflower seeds and served with cultured butter. I'm not especially into bread, but this was phenomenal.

Glidden Point oysters came next, with a nice 25% pinot blanc champagne. The oysters were small and sweet, served off the shell with pickled green gooseberries, swimming in a gooseberry vinaigrette dotted with juniper oil. Clean and refreshing--I think I low key drank up the vinaigrette like soup. The second bread was as good as the first: brown rolls made with malt and spices, rolled in fennel and caraway seeds, served with whipped pork fat dusted with dried yarrow powder. For the next course, we had the option to upgrade our roe to caviar for $50 a plate. We decided to stick with the roe, and I can't imagine this was a poor choice. The Vendace roe was spectacular, every tiny orange egg briny and bursting. It came with thin sticks of asparagus, asparagus powder and oil, lemon verbena, ramp capers, and a frothy sauce of fermented asparagus juice mixed with whey.

Our last seafood course was a silky, delicately meaty poached skate wing, plated with turnip purée, fire-roasted turnip glazed in lovage leaves, white currants, lovage purée, and a light green sauce made with smoked fish stock, white wine, and lovage oil. This was unbelievable, every element flawless and delicious. It came paired with a Napa Chardonnay. Our next wine was a palomino, described as somewhere between a white wine and a sherry. It accompanied a dish of fried reindeer moss with caramelized cream, pickled chanterelles, and spruce needles in a spruce vinegar and mushroom broth. I took a liking to this lichen, an unusual offering with a light, flossy texture and plenty of flavor, though some of that might have been the aromatic broth. For our final savory course, we had 120-day dry-aged beef, served with black and red currants, blackberry jam, and vinaigrette of berry juice and rendered beef fat. This was a perfect piece of meat, buttery and richly flavorful. I enjoyed it with a splash of pinot noir.

A lush, sweet 1994 chenin blanc took us through our desserts, which were, of course, fantastic. A clean, cool raw milk sorbet came with this year's wild strawberries and a fermented juice of last year's strawberries. Then, we had sweet, earthy birch bark ice cream with black trumpet and woodruff. Who knew mushrooms could go so well with ice cream?

The night closed with two bites of fudge: blood fudge dusted with rosehip, and white chocolate fudge with Swedish Punsch and sourdough malt powder. They tasted like nothing else I'd ever encountered. A fitting end to a dinner rich with marvels.
Really original menu and cuisine. The most inspired meal I've had in some time and service was impeccable, one of the best restaurants of the city,

3.5 stars for me, but will round up.  In summary, the experience was unique and memorable, but I wasn't the most excited about the actual food itself, especially considering the cost of the meal.

We had the 10-course abbreviated meal, and the biggest wow factor for me was the presentation, followed closely by the unique ingredients.  My favorite dishes included:

--2 bread courses (manitoba with oat and beer, spice roll): perfectly baked rolls, served piping hot with deliciously creamy butter...the way all bread service should be.
--oyster with green gooseberry, orpine, oil made with juniper needle: delicious sauce to go with the oyster.
--poached skate wing: very nicely prepared, with very tender fish and interesting complements and sauce (turnip glazed in lovage leaves, dill flower sauce)...too bad the skate was only one bite

With 10 courses, I didn't really walk away hungry (the boys in our group probably did though), but the portion sizes were on the small side, and 5/10 courses were either bread or dessert, which were probably the most filling dishes.  I was happy to have tried Aska for the beautiful and unique dining experience and did enjoy trying each course, but I don't think I would choose to come back here again, even for a special occasion.

We did the 12 course menu as we had a party of 6, and thus were in the private rolls in the back

As others have said, the food is incredibly inventive, delicious, and unique. It was a great culinary experience.

My rating though is based on two things:
-Our meal took FOREVER - literally four and a half hours. We weren't actually waiting that long between any particular course, it's just an incredibly long drawn out experience, so be prepared.

-The presentation and overall style of the restaurant is the height of pretension - talking about choosing wine as if it's supposed to be a transcendental spiritual experience, or describing how you picked the kolrabhi off a tree in a Williamsburg neighborhood garden down the block. The opposite of unpretentious, good food presented simply

It was a unique and worthwhile experience, but not one that left me wanting to come back, at least not unless I have another 5 hours to kill
Beautiful restaurant with great music. Food was spectacular. Razor clams on a bed of flowers and moss were my favorite. Mushroom ice cream was very different. Highly recommend

My wife and I had our anniversary dinner here this past week. It's been a spot I've been wanting to try for some time, and perhaps there's a little bit of bias involved as well (it is pronounced, if not exactly spelled, like my name). Even though both of us ran a little late, the hostess was more than gracious enough in getting us seated at our table. As the decor at the entrance suggests, Aska's ambiance tends towards the darker side, with an eclectic mix of decor hinting at the space's past - you have some brick walls, as well as some wooden pillars that look a little worse for wear and appear as though they had a bunch of papers taped onto them. There is a small cocktail menu available to choose some drinks from (my 'Wild Negroni' was alright, if not as inspiring as I had hoped), as well as a beverage pairing that you can choose to have. My wife went with the non-alcoholic pairing, which mixed in sodas and juices that I quite enjoyed (in particular, I liked the lingonberry juice and the herb-infused apple juice at the very end); my wine pairing was also decent, if a little bit less of a standout. My favorite was probably the mid-1990s vintage chenin blanc, which had sweetened considerably over time and was very nice as a dessert wine. Otherwise, the others tended to be wines that were a little off the beaten path (e.g. we had a number of Eastern European white wines) - fine overall, but perhaps not as memorable. I also think the timing of the beverages could be a bit more even; as we got towards the end of the meal, the table started filling up with multiple glasses for each of us.
