The tasting menu clocked in at 16 'courses', although unlike some restaurants that follow a similar length (e.g. Chef's Table at Brooklyn Fare), the first few bites were more like amuse-bouche, and the two bread servings are also counted among the courses. Not unsurprisingly given the Scandinavian influences, there is a lot of focus on herbs reflected in a number of the dishes. Shrimp heads - more of an Asian delicacy - is booked with dill and lamb fat and actually is probably the most delicious iteration of this that I have had, in large part perhaps (because?) the very inky, harsh flavor of the brain is either well-covered or removed entirely. Langoustine is served encased in smoked juniper sprigs that you cut open - imparting a nice, faintly woodsy aroma to the meat without being overpowering. Maine oysters are served already shucked and served cool with juniper-infused oil - a very light but delicious pairing. One of my favorite bites was the skate wing, which you pull off the fish bone and dip into the dill-infused sauce - another fantastic bite on its own as well. The quail is served with a lot of pine sprigs around it (and is cooked with pine-infused butter), which I did enjoy but was also a bit on the small side. What really hit the mark for me were the desserts. I'm a strawberry fan, so getting a milk sorbet served with strawberries in fermented (yet still sweet) strawberry juice was a cool, refreshing way to start off the sweet portion of the meal. The birchwood ice cream was even better, though - it was drenched in what came off as relatively unsweetened maple-like syrup, and the candied mushrooms on the top really rounded off a sweet but very forest-y course.

Some dishes, though, while interesting, didn't quite hit the same mark for me. The kohlrabi was literally a slice of the vegetable, served as what looked like a very thin slice of apple. While it's a much different take on it (as I am used to boiling / mashing this down, a la a potato), to count that as a course - or really an interesting bite - would be pushing it. The lichen (or 'reindeer moss') had a fun, crackly texture, but it was quite plain on its own. The bread courses were both pretty good, but it didn't stand out compared to some of the other breads I have enjoyed elsewhere.

Overall, I'd likely come back for another meal. I really enjoyed the approach to the meal, and if there's one thing that was always executed well, it was just how good-looking all of the food was when each course came out. That said, I wasn't as blown away by the time we had finished compared to another high-end Scandinavian spot in NYC (Aquavit), and the meal goes a (very) long time...it was closer to 4(!) hours by the time we were finished. It's a great experience overall, though, and if you have the time and the money for it, Aska is worth the visit.

Ok so let me get the only one negative thing out of the way. We had an 8pm reservation and the meal ended at 12:45. No meal should take that long and we did get really tired towards the end. 

That being said let me tell you about one of the best food experiences I have ever enjoyed. My partner and I have dined at what are considered some of the best restaurants across the world such as Gaggan, Quintonnil, Steirereck and many more and I have to say when it came to the actual food it was top 2-3 meal we have ever enjoyed. This is truly food perfection! All 16-20 courses depending on how you count them we're above expectations and 80% were excellent/mind blowing. I cannot stress enough that if you live in NYC or visiting you must make a stop here. Pair it with a bottle or two of wine from their extensive natural wine bottle list.

It sort of pains me to right this review since I took my boyfriend here for his birthday as a surprise - he had wanted to go here for a while since we had both heard extremely positive things about Aska.

Unfortunately, to our disappointment Aska did not impress. Let's start with the long wait time - if I am dining at a 2 Michelin starred restaurant and paying $$$$ for a meal, I do not expect to have to wait 30 minutes before being seated. I did not mind the length of our meal (we did the long format 19 courses, so the meal took several hours), but I think having to wait that long to be seated is unacceptable.

As for the food, we enjoyed roughly 1/2 of the items, with only about 1/3 of them blowing us away. Again, for a restaurant of this calibre, I expect to have a memorable meal and not be served forgettable dishes. In addition, I believe the servers could have provided a bit more description about what exactly they were serving us. In my mind, a tasting menu such as this is a story, an epic even, with each dish being a chapter which enchants you even more as you progress. 

One of the few positives was the sommelier introducing us to a funky Hungarian wine which we enjoyed. We had described the type of wine we wanted to try, and she came back with a rather surprising choice which turned out to be a highlight of the meal. 

A thoroughly disappointing experience overall; I don't think I'll be coming back to Aska :(

We had a 7:30 reservation for the long format dinner. 
First course was seaweed Bladderwrack interesting but unimpressive to me. Potato pancake was delicious. Kohlrabi my partner really liked but I found uninventive. I wished it wasn't one big hunk of cold kohlrabi. I didn't need a refreshing dish this early in the meal I wanted something heartier. Shrimp was also a disappointing course unfortunately, the rose petal ravioli were so little I could barely taste them. The flavors were there but this dish was so tiny. For the first four courses to be basically less than a bite I was disappointed. 
Manitoba bread course was incredible. Langoustine course was interesting. Loved the herbs and sauce on the side, the langoustine was only "half-smoked" which left it strangely squishy and half raw. Flavors were all on point though. Oyster was an odd dish. None of it came together for me. My partner wasn't a fan either. Another bread course with whipped pork fat, excellent. 
Now after the first half of the meal I liked pretty much every dish. Usually restaurants put out their best courses first. But I was much more impressed with the second half. 
Lettuce root dish with caviar and whey asparagus sauce was amazing. Stand out dish. Stunning and unique. Cucumber with razor clams was a beautiful presentation and delicious combination of flavors. Quail with truffles was fabulous. I enjoyed the bonus snack too. Lichen was creative and surprisingly tasty. Definitely never eaten anything like it before. Skate dish was maybe my favorite. The sauce was absolutely delicious. Loved the addition of white currants. 
Strawberry dessert was incredible. Raw milk sorbet was one of my favorite cold desserts maybe ever and I normally dislike ice cream. the fermented strawberry juice was a perfect accompaniment. Birchwood ice cream with pine mushrooms, candied black trumpets, and birch woodruff syrup was the last dessert. One of the most unique dishes I've ever tasted. 
I would say I was impressed with half the dishes. About six were total stand outs. Food presentation was 5/5 and I'd say taste was 4/5. Service was lovely. There was only one dish I disliked (Oyster). Rachel served us and she was excellent. The space is beautiful and large. I liked that all the chairs faced the open kitchen.

Just had an amazing dinner.  Our 8 course meal was a magical combination of salt and sweet.  My family's food roots are scandinavian.  Aska's chef made a great onderful combination of familiar and modern.  I relished each course.

Kinda disappointed actually. 3.5-4 star to me. I had a very high expectation for this Scandinavian Michelin 2-star restaurant, but the result actually turned out to be just around average level. I went there in summer time around May in party of three. We opted the 16-course tasting menu, however both of my friends and I felt not full after the dinner..

The place located in Brooklyn, a long way from the city to go. But given the reputation, it's still worth going. The ambiance and the waiter services are perfect 5 starts, very decent and elegant with the dark tablecloth. We had a window seating table, where we saw the sunset during the dinner, from daylight to night. The food itself, honestly I felt at an average level, and portion is pretty small. The 16-course (13 dishes, 3 desserts): The Manitoba is very special, with oat and beer and cultured butter. I also like the Oyster, with green gooseberry, orpine, oil made with juniper needle. The quail is great as well, it's roasted, from Vermont with summer truffle. The white asparagus with caviar is one of my fav dish. I do not like Langoustine, tasted weird and dry... But I do love the desserts here, the strawberry milk sorbet, birchwood ice cream, caramelized white chocolate, all perfect.

I think the meat, ingredients here are all at decent level, but the sauce or the cooking style is not something I expected. But the service and setting does worth a try.

First time to see the bread comes with pork fat.

Came here on our wedding day with my husband.  I was so glad I chose Aska for my special day. The tasting menu provided us a great feast that night. The dishes were tasting and creative and even looks like an art. I was satisfied with all of them.

A very neat environment in Brooklyn. Their dishes are arts, really beautiful. Even though the taste is nothing surprised. 
The deserts and ice cream is good though.

The exquisite attention to detail on every bite is what makes this such an exciting experience.
We loved the freshness of the ingredients and the total surprise in the flavors.
Definitely one for the bucket list.

Had an incredible time in the garden, with the bar menu. Uncrowded, great vibe, and no reservations needed (or taken).

Drinks were fantastic, service was always there when we needed it but invisible when we didn't. Highlights included the oysters, the carrots, and the smoked hake.
Just went here for a drink in the bar downstairs. Pricey but a lovely setting, good drink menu, smooth service.

Been here for dinner course once and wine tasting twice. It's a small modern Scandinavian space. I really liked their blue mussels! My mom didn't like the food here much because she thinks it's too light. She has always been preferring heavier ingredients and sauce. But if you like light food, you should try here! For the other two times here for wine tasting, I have to say their small bites were amazing even though the wine choices were less strong. Also I think the tasting this year almost doubled last year's price which I think is little over priced for their wine tasting event. In general I would recommend this place for dinner but not their wine tasting event if it's $150 like this year.

KenScale: 9.0/10

The last time I visited Aska with my wife Jun (who was still my girlfriend then) a couple of years ago in the winter, there was snow blizzard on our way to the restaurant. We were heading over to Williamsburg from downtown Manhattan so obvious the ride wasn't quite pleasant, but I was very glad we ended up making the trip anyway as the meal that we shared was one of the best we had had together. In the quest (starting this year) to find restaurants that we would plan to go more than just once, I thought of Aska as one of the strong candidates. Of course, the tasting menu price at $265 per person (to be secured by $95 non-refundable deposit on Tock website) doesn't make the restaurant a place to visit every day, but if the menu changes on a seasonal basis, I figured it could be one of those places that Jun and I can go three to four times a year (just like I recently designated Atomix as one such place on the KenScale All Star list). I'm happy to report that our second meal at Aska was just as memorable and I'm ready to give the KenScale All Star badge to the restaurant.

The tasting menu at Aska has certainly gone up in price (last time I had the 10-course tasting at the restaurant, it was $145 per person), but it was clear that chef Fredrik Berselius's kitchen doesn't settle or play safe even after the restaurant has gained accolades left and right. The plating, starting from the opening bladderwrak with blue mussel emulsion, and ending with the petit fours of "mignardises", was just as thoughtful as last time, and the addition to flowers here and there greatly enhanced the visual appeal as well. If I wake up with a bite of potato cake with roe smoked in dried carrot tops and elderflower every morning, I will certainly start my day a much happier person. The razor clam with tiny slices of preserved black pine and cucumber was one fine piece of work, and the textural contrast between the caviar from Poland and the dried cabbage submerged in the sauce made from fermented asparagus juice was quite outstanding as well. You don't often see the tiny brain part of langoustine used in a restaurant, but that's what the kitchen sent out, alongside the tail and claw meat; Jun thought the brain was a little too buttery but I liked its rich flavor. Following another outstanding dish of grilled onion and scallop and the warm Manitoba bread accompanied by butter and whipped pork fat came my best dish of the night, a perfectly poached hake with sunchoke; I was astounded by the silky smooth texture of the fish that was melting in my mouth and contrasted very well with the sunchoke's texture. I don't usually get quail for a meat dish because it doesn't have the same satisfaction in texture that other types of poultry provide, but I had no compliant about the roasted bird (with a rather intimidating display of feet) with summer truffle. After the end of the savory dishes, the black currant tart with fresh cheese served as a nice palate cleanser before we moved to ice cream made from toasted hay and summer flowers that was quite a treat to end the meal.

Because getting a reservation at Aska requires the non-refundable deposit mentioned above and the restaurant is still quite popular among fine dining aficionados in the city, I would highly recommend advance planning to secure your table. There is full bar with rather esoteric list of wines (we really enjoyed a pinot noir from Oregon outside of the famed Willamette Valley that developed quite nicely in the air over the course of our meal) from lesser-known regions of the world. It was almost two and a half years ago that Jun and I had visited Aska, so we were greatly surprised by the greeting from our server who noted our previous visit; even chef Fredrik who we had taken photos together last time came by to say hi. I couldn't be sure if anyone working at the restaurant remembered us (even though we were probably the only people that still made it to the restaurant despite the horrible weather outside last time), but the extra gesture of hospitality certainly helped with my impression of Aska even more. As we headed out of the restaurant, Jun and I promised our server that we will be back sometime in November. And we certainly will.

Loved almost every single bite I had here. Other than gravlax and IKEA meatballs, I'd never had Scandinavian cuisine before, so this was certainly an amazing introduction. 

Out of the tasting menu the courses that stick out most in my mind even a month later as I'm writing this are the bladderwrack (laugh at the name but it's a delicious seaweed chip) and the lobster brain/claw/tail combination. But I could just as easily rave over the potato pancake, or the beer bread (the "correct" description is Manitoba loaves leavened with IPA, but let's be real, it's just beer bread) accompanied by butter and whipped pork lard, or the savoury af quail and black truffle dish. I loved it all! Even the ones that weren't my personal favourites - razor clams, osetra caviar and peas, hake - were still beautiful in both taste and presentation. 

My table's least liked course by far was the blackberry tart that was the first dessert - there was something about it that straight up tasted rancid and bitter, and most of us couldn't finish our tarts, small as they already were. But the other two desserts were incredible - toasted hay ice cream with meadowsweet-filled aebleskiver, and a piece of bark with several candies on top. Probably the only time in my life I'll try something as interesting as their blood truffle. 

If you come, I HIGHLY recommend the juice pairing! It's definitely unique - how many high-end juice pairings have you come across in your life? - and I couldn't pass up the chance. Our selection came with ones like Douglas fir, rhubarb soda with rose vinaigrette, huckleberry spruce, bronze fennel blossom, etc. I didn't like all of them but absolutely don't regret such a one-of-a-kind experience like that. If you opt for alcohol instead, don't sleep on their many choices of aquavit. 

Service is impeccable, as to be expected. There's also a lovely garden in the back and a basement bar downstairs - the space is unexpectedly large. And don't worry if you don't catch or understand some of the waiters when they explain the courses - you'll get a take home menu at the end.

I'll absolutely be back to try their winter menu!

Small portions but delicious. Dishes are very social media friendly. More impressive with pics than the actual setting, but still minimalist chic. I didn't do the wine pairing after reading a few reviews and I'm glad I didn't. Wine selection is fair, but the dishes are appetizer portions so no need to pair each with a glass of wine.
I celebrated my birthday last week at Aska with a few friends. I didn't find any of the dishes I had to be particularly delicious.

Aska require a higher level of appreciation, normal diner would find hard to understand either the concept or the cuisine. Many unusual and rare ingredients were used, and most important, they worked perfectly with each other, it's very precious in a contemporary cuisine.

My husband and I came here for my birthday this year on a Friday night.  We had a great experience, with wonderful service and great food. 

We came 30 minutes early or so to enjoy a drink on their back patio - which is very cute with string lights and nice greenery.  The floor out there is pebbles so be careful with your heels if you are wearing any.

We saw that they had a corkage fee (I think it was $75) so we brought a nice bottle of wine with us to enjoy with our meal - we had a cocktail before outside on the patio as mentioned and then a glass of champagne inside the dining room, and then a couple after dinner drinks (we splurged and ordered ones that were $60 per glass (I think it was a 1977 Madeira) because why not). 

The presentation of the food was really neat and quite beautiful.  The flavors were on point and ingredients fresh.  The one course I did not really care for, which our server warned us about, was the lobster brain - the consistency was quite gross for me. Other than that, the dishes were really unique and we enjoyed them all.

The Aska menu definitely felt experimental to me and my taste buds, and I usually boast about how I'm adventurous with food.

I think this is my first time trying Scandinavian food, and unsurprisingly it's seafood heavy. My favorites were the Hake, Quail, and Potato Pancake. The Langoustine (lobster) brain was definitely an interesting course, and the tail was so good that I'm salivating just thinking about it. Because it was my friend's birthday, we were comped with mini donuts (I forget the name), which tasted very similar to corn bread and I miss them very much.

Thank you for a wonderful 2-star Michelin experience - it was definitely unforgettable.

Third time to this two-Michelin-Star restaurant. But this time, despite increasing the price quite a bit, bread is no longer complimentary, but actually considered one of the courses in this multi course tasting menu. Though every dish is out of this world delicious, when we got home I needed a bowl of spaghetti and my wife ate almost two bags of jerky before we were satiated. I wish more bread were given. Too bad.

New favorite 2-star Michelin restaurant in NY (price point aside)!  Excellent sommelier and service; eclectic and beautiful artsy cuisine. Balanced gastronomy.  Wow'ed by the Langostine course (brains in its own broth, followed by perfectly grilled medium rare Tails) and the poached Hake (in its own bone-broth emulsion paired with seaweed/kelp and herbs). The quail course was the weakest link- too much sauce (could've done without) and the side was salty.  

All-in price (with wines) is on par with 3-star restaurants, but you leave with more room in your stomach and surprisingly no gift bag.  We celebrated my birthday and was disappointed the only addition to the meal was a candle- no complimentary toast or desserts/gifts like other top restaurants.  Overall, we loved the unique tasting menu but felt the evening was missing a few touches.

The most delicious, delicate, imaginative food. Exquisite dining but with an authentic, friendly and easy atmosphere. Tasting menu was the perfect amount. Wonderful being able to see the chefs at work in the kitchen. And the best cocktail I've ever had (couldn't find the name on their website, it contained a chanterelle vinegar among other delights). Overall price may be just for special occasions for sure, but we'll be back at least for a cocktail at the bar.

Such a wonderful restaurant! 
It was our anniversary and we wanted to have something special this day. So I've read a lot of comments and choose Aska. 
Food was amazing. We loved everything. Service also was nice. No complaints. 
I like the way they've presented every dish, it wasn't waiters. Cooks did it. And every time it was different person.

The only one thing I didn't like was cocktails. Not tasty at all. Drinkable but it's not what you are expecting from such an expensive restaurant. But still we enjoyed our dinner and experience in total. Definitely will recommend it to my friends.

I love it. We met the chef here and their food is super nicely curated. Fresh taste, magic combination, beautiful! I started to understand why the food are plated like it is after seeing the chef - he's from Stockholm :p
A truly unique and creative experience to enjoy food. The menu conceptualization is simply genius.

Overall, good experience, but very expensive. One of my friends summed this experience up the best, "a little twig, a little broth, a little protein"

Scandinavian food is not something I have often, so it was worth trying something new. I'm not sure I'd come back for a second time, but it's definitely a spot you should try at least once if you're a foodie

Last time I was in Scandinavia (Goteborg in Sweden to be exact) the $550 that I dropped for 2 people in Aska in Brooklyn would have lasted for at least a month at one of the many great restaurants in the Brunnsparken district.

The Scandinavian inspired food at Aska on 5th Street in Brooklyn is tasty, tiny and massively overpriced. I say inspired, because through my travels in Scandinavia there was a lot of herring and this place did not even have it on the menu.

You will often leave this gorgeous restaurant feeling really hungry after eating only about 300 calories of beautiful food. It works out to be about a $1 per calorie. If you want 1000 calories,  that will be $1000 please. The bar scene pre-covid was fun, but only dining is available right now, so time to break out the Amex Black card or burn through little timmy's college fund if you want to eat and drink.

Post-Covid, the excesses of restaurants like Aska seem out of context in our modern time and its a bit of a throwback to the excess of the pre-covid years. Much like the excesses of a Roman Toga party, the fortunes of this restaurant will ultimately dim. People have begun to recognize that this kind of excess is not just de riguer, but it is now deemed objectionable in the Post Covid landscape. It will be a shame to see it go, but it will surely end. You cant charge $1 per calorie and expect people to pay it post-Covid, regardless of how good the tiny lamb heart looks.

Food was ok and it was good experience. They pay more attention to presentation and performance than taste of the dish. 
And be careful. They might ask you if you want to add truffle for $110 each per person, but pronounce it like $10. Greate marketing trick.

Two months into the second Covid reopening, and Aska has obviously hit the ground running.  For the smaller lunch menu, I was treated to three hours of excellent atmosphere, service and, of course, food.

While I've only been to maybe a half-dozen Michelin restaurants in Scandinavian countries, the otherwise highly enjoyable menu presented here in Williamsburg seemed a lot more of an "inspired-by" than "authentic-recipe-of," and somewhat altered my expectations.

That aside, I truly enjoyed the razor clam/ cucumber réduction amuse bouche and the celeriac/ truffle/ dried venison that accompanied the excellent roast venison, and of course, the bedstraw ice cream/ meadowsweet caramel.

I must return very soon.

2021 04 10. M2.

Aska has wowed my fiancé and I! From service, to presentation, to all the details in their delectable tasting and their quality cocktails. 

I actually think for the price you pay it lives up to their impeccable quality. I think pictures worth a thousand words, so I'll let that speak for itself. 

P.S. these dishes look simple but will send your taste buds through the roof. I also didn't take pictures of all the dishes, nevertheless we were very pleased.
Creatively curated menu in a Scandinavian inspired interior design setting.  Every dish was flawlessly executed, and the in-house sommelier was very knowledgeable.

Great place with 12 courses of fantastic food.  The chefs present each dish and there are some table side preparations.  I'd definitely go back as it is worth the price.  There needs to be a some refinement in the service and the chefs presentations, but great experience.

Glad I made reservations far enough in advance. This Michelin 2 Star'd restaurant really lived up to the hype.

Cozy dining room that was very welcoming, our server was so fun and knowledgeable.

What I found out later was that there is an option to pair the vegetable drinks with the food. I got to try a couple and was blown away! Was kicking myself for not reading the fine print on the tasting menu.

Fantastic experience and will for sure be back!

Aska was definitely a memorable experience and I'm glad I got to experience it.  There were some missteps with some of the dishes, but all in all they were delicious- especially those dessert truffles!  I appreciate that they were accommodating of the fact that my lovely friend came a little late and still let us sit and enjoy the meal.  When the table was needed for another party, they graciously accommodated with a table outside.  The reason I gave 4 stars VS 5 stars is I felt that some of the dishes weren't what I had expected them to be but all in all it's definitely an experience worth having.

Excellent lunch pre fix menu. This restaurant stands out in the way that Jungsik, in NY, and Atica, in Australia, have stood out. The attention to detail was apparent and the kitchen executed all of the dishes perfectly. I can't wait to return and experience the dinner menu.

Loved the consistent use of edible flowers and flavorful liquids. Enjoyed the first dish (on kelp) and ice cream dessert less than other courses. Food arrived at a comfortable pace; usually a few minutes between each of 14 courses and about a half-dozen paired drinks. As aesthetic as it was delicious, to the extent that, for a few courses, it seemed premature for the servers to immediately cover the artpiece with sauce/etc. Maybe a solution is to ask the customer whether they'd want to pour it themselves. Nonetheless, impeccable coordinated service. Environment and scenery feel NYC-esque (more condensed and low-key than one may expect). Overall an impressive, unique, unforgettable meal. Aska deserves its stars: both Michelins and the 5 I give it.

Sat down at 7:30pm on a Thursday (group of 8 people). "Dinner" took ~4.5hrs. John (tall bald gentlemen) should evaluate his demeanor towards guests paying $500 per person and pay attention to requests/details. When a restaurant asks about dietary restrictions and then bluntly ignores such restrictions- a piece of your soul dies. Icing on the cake (or lack there of) was being chases out into the street for a larger tip.

Continuing on our fine dining journey, we decided to finally give this restaurant a try. They have definitely proven to be creative with all their dishes. the amount of effort in each dish and the fine details were evident in the presentation. As for the taste, a lot of the dishes are interesting. Interesting in the way that we were like woah what is this? This is a new blend of flavors in my mouth.  And we couldn't register a oh we love this or an oh this is odd but I guess good or maybe just odd. Regardless, we had a great time. We left quite hungry and ready for our second dinner. Street parking wasn't too bad that night.

Amazing service, awesome food and amazing attention to dietary restriction! I'm gf and they made gf bread/ sweets for me so I don't miss out! Everything was interesting and I loved 90% of everything I tried (I'm really picky too)! My first Scandinavian food tasting journey and so glad I came here for this! Will be back!

What an experience! Each bite got better and better with a presentation that can't be beat. I really enjoyed not knowing the menu before hand and being surprised as each item arrived to the table. 
The restaurant is small with a dark simple Scandinavian feel (in a great way). Large outdoor patio that I will definitely be back for come Spring.

Notes: 
Team members: great! 
Corkage fee: $100
This place is absolutely amazing! Worth every penny! Got the wine pairing alongside the menu. I was blown away by the food. So many flavors. One of my favorite meals!

Dining at Aska was my first time having Nordic cuisine.  I know it has been the hot thing for the last decade or so but I really was just not interested.  The idea of eating mosses and things didn't sound appetizing to me; I am glad I finally tried it though.  Although there might be some moss like items, they certainly aren't the main event and they actually do add interest to the dishes.  The menu is an extensive tasting menu 12 plus courses and all were creatively presented, contained numerous complimentary ingredients and were delicious.  The entire meal was certainly a journey and experience that left know doubt that the young chef and his team spend endless amounts of time planning, creating and plating each spectacular course.  We had the wine pairings which were masterfully matched with the courses.  I would highly recommend giving Aska a try if you can get in.

My boyfriend and I had such an amazing experience dining at Aska. Everything was impeccable--from their service, to their wine and food. 

The only thing I would point out is the hours on the website and Yelp was a bit strange. The restaurant said it was closed at 8:45 but our reservation was at 9. I've made my reservation about a month ago and wasn't sure how to reach out to confirm since they didn't pick up their phone.

Luckily when we arrived, the restaurant was open and we were relieved. The tables were all full so I understood that they were busy and was unable to pick up. 

To conclude, I definitely enjoyed everything! They catered to us and made sure we were happy. Loved this experience and will definitely come back again soon!

My wife and I had dinner on a Friday night.  The food was great, and in particular the grilled langoustine and the scallops were truly amazing. Our biggest complaint was the serving tempo- we sat down at 8:45pm which was our reservation time, ordered a drink each which was promptly served, but then... the first dish did not come out until it was nearly 9:50pm. As many others here have noted, it took nearly three hours to finish the meal.  No matter how good the food was, we were pretty worn out by the end, given it was nearly midnight.  The desserts were also underwhelming, consisting mostly of cookie-type food that was okay, but not really the level you would expect at a two Michelin-star restaurant.

This place is simply incredible. Such a fun and unique experience! Each bite melts in your mouth and pairs perfectly with all of the wines they serve you. I love how they have an open kitchen so that you can see the chefs preparing your food. The sommeliers are also very attentive and make sure that you are properly fed and wined. I love how dark the restaurant is as well. Perfect for a fancy, romantic date night.

Pros:  Great service by the wait staff and sommelier.  Modern and minimalist décor with an open kitchen, brick walls painted black and black floors, tablecloths and chairs illuminated by table oil lamps.  There were some truly unique and innovate dishes with beautiful presentation. I particularly enjoyed the venison preparation, which was succulent and rich, as opposed to the gamey versions I've had in the past.
 
Cons:  The overall flavor profile of the dishes (apart from the venison) was mild and muted, despite the freshness of the ingredients.  I was more impressed with the dishes at Aquavit, another Michelin rated Scandinavian restaurant.  I was particularly turned off by the substitutions they utilized for my dinner date, who could not eat lobster or crab.  The restaurant was informed of his dietary restrictions beforehand.  Instead of supplying him with another fish protein, they served him a stick of asparagus for one dish and another vegetable for another dish.  A meal with a $1.2K price tag should have better substitutions.  We were both still hungry after our meal, and stopped by McDonalds on the way home.

Beyond every course on the tasting menu being truly impeccable, as if my taste buds went on vacation to five-star resort, I would love to attest to the storytelling of the staff. Specifically Missy  (Melissa) - her whimsical style enhanced the taste and experience of the evening. Not only was she informative, but her personality shined through her descriptions and various anecdotes on the winemaster. With that being said, the entire staff was superb. 

Sure, the food was splendid, but the energy, the palpable tender love and care paid to each guest, the fine point attention to detail -- this is what resonated with me most. 

I give this restaurant five stars, but I wish I could give it five more.

Food was very beautiful and everything was tasty. Some things were superb. wonderful service. Not filling at all though and left hungry. My friend and I got McDonald's afterwards :/ it was nice, but I feel no need to go back. I know it's a fine dining experience and the point is not to leave feeling stuffed, but for the amount of money you pay it would be nice to get more food.

Celebrated my boyfriend's birthday at Aska and had an amazing experience. Service was great and everything we ate was impeccable.

The tasting was hit after hit - seafood, venison, lichen! - and beautifully presented. The far north Negroni cocktail and the first rule cocktail were both awesome, too.

Definitely recommended for a unique tasting experience, especially if you've already collected all the French Michelin infinity stones in this city.

Appearance without substance. The art of high cuisine is to combine presentation, taste, and texture. They got the presentation but seem to have forgotten about the taste and texture. All show and pretense, without the actual pleasure. I've dined at most 2 and 3 Michelin starred restaurants in NYC and this was the worst.

Celebrated a special dinner last night and everything was excellent. Compared to the most recent two-Michelin starred restaurant we went to (Jungsik), Aska blows them out of the water. Nearly every dish was executed wonderfully with complex and interesting flavors. The wine pairing was very nice and the sommelier (Missy) was absolutely great.  Read the (many) reviews that say people leave hungry after the tasting menu, so we had a little snack before dinner. Whether the snack was what held us over or not, I'm not sure but I felt satisfied at the end of our evening.

What an adventurous dinner in this all-black restored 1860s warehouse in Brooklyn! From my seat, I gazed at the open kitchen filled with chefs like scientists conducting experiments. Their thoughtful collaboration is the backbone of the dreamy and ethereal dishes, which held bold, experimental, and excellent Scandinavian flavors from the ocean, seasoned gently. 

The meal began with 3 bite-sized snacks -- dried bladderwrack seaweed dotted with blue mussel emulsion, kohlrabi (german turnip) compressed with linden leaf oil and linden flower vinegar, and a mini tart with vendace roe marinated in horseradish oil and lilac vinegar. I loved the tart; each bite was filled with brimy and crunchy tiny orange eggs, and the flaky tart shell nicely supplemented it. 

My favorite dishes were the 1) grilled langoustine tail from Norway with sauce from caramelized shells and red gooseberry and 2) light custard with smoked eel, salted spruce and spring shoots. the orange-pink langoustine tail was strikingly fresh and sweet, and so tender. the custard reminded me of Japanese Chawanmushi, with a smoky twist.

The portions, however, were on the smaller side and I found myself not full afterwards but maybe that's just a part of savoring works of art. Overall, I was still very satisfied with the experience and outstanding service.

Yum! Came here for my birthday dinner 6/2022 and loved it. The all black aesthetic really set the mood and the kitchen was the main focal point. Everyone worked in perfect synchronization and the staff didn't miss a beat. Food was spectacular. Very creative presentation and unique flavors. The Langoustine from Norway was immaculate it will definitely be a dish I will remember for a very long time. Would come back again! This restaurant completed my journey of trying all the 3 and 2 Michelin star restaurants in NY and I must say this was overall a very memorable one!
Impeccable and intriguing. Beautiful service start to finish. 10/10 recommend this experience

Date Visited: August 2022
More Reviews on Instagram: @angelicfoodie_
Dinner Tasting Menu w/ Wine Pairing
Everything (including bathroom) was 10/10!

I couldn't have asked for a more perfect birthday dinner!  It was an adventure for the tastebuds, and is now one of my favorite restaurants! 
Aska is perfect for special occasions! We left full, satisfied, and a little tipsy 
The flavor of each dish was complex and unique. If the server didn't explain each dish to us, we would've had difficulty distinguishing the ingredients. Each dish was thoughtfully plated. Service was attentive and efficient. 
We ordered cocktails which were well balanced but unnecessary since we did the wine pairing. And I highly recommend the wine pairing! 
My favorite dishes were:
- Caviar (w/ king fish, smoked eel, green gooseberry and juniper)
- Languistine (w/ sauce of caramelized shells and red gooseberry)
- Hake (w/ young onion and albino sturgeon caviar, flowering dill and Swedish dark beer) 
Favorite wine was the Carignan Blanc Domaine Ledogar 2018. It paired well with the food but I would also enjoy drinking this by itself  The sake, Ine Mankai from Mukai Shuzo, was an interesting addition and paired well with the Langoustine. 
Opportunities: 
- We had difficulty hearing the sommelier
- 2019 Clement Baraut La Lune de Beltaine did not pair as well with the Hake dish

TLDR: incredible experience, may be my favorite meal yet (Michelin starred) and would 100% recommend.

My boyfriend took me to Aska for my birthday on a Friday night at 8:30pm.  The restaurant is minimal and dark, with cool black furniture and little accents for decoration. There is an open kitchen surrounded by a higher than waist height wall, where you can kind of see all the action. The place has only a handful of tables so everything is spaced nicely apart and you almost feel like you're watching a private (cooking) show with just a small group of people. 

SETTING: perfect for a special occasion. I loved the space and how it wasn't overcrowded with tables.

FOOD: the food was incredible, and may be one of my favorite meals ever. I can't remember the nuances and details of each dish, but I do know that everything was really unique, flavorful, playful and done to perfection. Most of the savory courses were fish based with one meat dish. 

VERDICT: I usually am a one and done fine diner, I don't see the need to go back to Michelin starred restaurants but Aska may be the only one that's changed that stance. Even writing this review, my mouth is watering, and I can't wait for the next special occasion to come back.

Enjoyed a magnificent dinner at Aska on Thursday evening. Well-deserving of its Michelin stars and constant praise, as the precision in both the food and the service is second to none.

Quality: Creativity and richness define the Tasting Menu we enjoyed. Every dish showcasing technical skills and thoughtfulness. Throughout the evening it was the sauces and foams that garnered the strongest reactions from my group. A white asparagus foam and a dill sauce were two standouts. The freshness of the seafood and the precision for the venison were also amazing. The ability to serve the venison without any toughness or gaminess was awe-inspiring. I will pick the Lobster course as my favorite, but the Hake and Vension are close behind. Though there was not a single dish that could be complained about and wasn't part of the adventure.
Quantity: The Tasting Menu came with 14 courses over the three hour journey. A perfect pacing ensures you feel satisfied and never over full.
Value: $295 for the Tasting Menu.
Ambiance: Aska is located in Williamsburg under the shadow of the Williamsburg Bridge. On an unassuming side street the space has a black exterior with little indication of the wonders inside. The inside area has a similar dark appearance, with any non-brick walls, ceiling, and tables draped in black. It is dim with lights showcasing where plates are placed, and in the kitchen towards the center of the dining room. The kitchen was nearly silent throughout the evening, which was so unexpected and clearly requires tremendous practice. The only oddity was an 80s pop and rock playlist that played quietly in the background, I think a more classical or ambient playlist would have fit the vibe a little better.
Crowd: Reservations are required, I would suggest at minimum two to three weeks before.
Service: Perfection. The knowledge and skill needed to ensure every element of the meal comes together is unbelievably impressive. Each staff member was courteous and helpful, and the way they were able to accommodate allergies in our party was tremendous. A synchronized event that looks so effortless, but requires tons of work.
Parking: Some nearby street parking in this area near the bridge.

One of the best and creative restaurants in NY (actually Brooklyn).
Around 14 small bites, each one is better than the other.
Both the ingredients, cooking, accommodated foam / soup to each dish were amazing.
Every dish was delivered by one of the cooks.
Around 250 usd per tasting menu.
200 usd for the wine pairing, one of the most interesting and creative wine tasting. And the sommelier was so nice, and explanatory.

It's a 2 michelin star. But we has a 3 star experience.

One to come back

Totally deserving of the two Michelin stars they have held for years. Was excited to finally try it and I was not let down. Aska is kind of aquavits hip moody little brother who lives in Brooklyn. The dark interior can seem oppressive but the lighting really lets the food shine. Tidy efficient kitchen is in sight and the staff is super attentive. Neve waited for anything! It's prolly better they make you pay ahead that way you can just focus on the food. And I would be lying if I said it was expensive. It is and yes you may leave a little hungry. But, personally I felt fine and not like a stuffed pig by the end. This is quality over quantity and I am ok with that. The neo-Scandinavian food is seafood heavy. But, each bit is refreshing and flavorful and unique. Inspired sauces and flavors drawn from nature rather than pounding the food with spices. This really lets the ingredients sing. I left pictures and am not going to say what was best, because every dish was solid. In fact what was most impressive was that the meal built. Each dish flowed into the next and in a way was better then the last. It was a truly harmonious meal. Worth the splurge for a special occasion. Only wish is that they had liquor and cocktails but not a big deal.

One of the best dining experiences of my life. The food was delicious and beautifully prepared. You could taste that thought and care that went into each plate. Honestly the best wine pairing I've had since moving to NYC. Highly recommend.

Incredible! 

We had the pleasure of visiting Aska, this past year, and we fell in love! 

The staff went above and beyond to welcome my wife and I, even coming out of the prep area, as we were leaving, to thank us for coming in and wish us a happy anniversary. 

The attention to detail was top notch, and I really enjoyed how attentive the staff was to our individual experience. Even going to the bathroom you are treated to a refreshing of your dining space upon your return. 

I need to preface the food review by saying that my wife and I had a healthy skepticism toward the food and the price of it all. Some of the dishes were well outside of our comfort zones, but we put our trust in Aska, and were blown away at each step. The flavor and texture profiles always complimented each other to form unique and exquisite experiences. There were more than a few times when the dishes created a sensation on the palate the was quite difficult to describe, basically eliciting a literal mouth euphoria.

We hesitantly opted for the juice pairing, when booking, even though it seemed very pricey for mere juice, and are so glad that we did. The combinations that they concocted were highly uncommon, visually interesting, and positively unforgettable. So many interesting flavors that I would never have imagined would work so well together. 

Thank you, Aska, for creating such wonderfully unique and unforgettable experiences.

The food was good and the chef was great, but I went with 3 of my friends (all girls) and had the most bizarre, rude experience from who I'm assuming was the restaurant manager (tall white  bald guy, dark facial hair). This happened last June and I've debated writing this review because it doesn't reflect the food or our service from anyone else there. But I will say because of this experience I will never return and it honestly ruined what should've been a great night for us. 

In the very beginning of the meal I accidentally knocked over my wine while showing my friend a picture on my phone. I'm 5'10 and am very long and clumsy. Mind you, this was our first round of drinks as we had just gotten there and none of us were drunk or being loud or rowdy. I profusely apologized while they cleaned up the wine and they didn't seem to care so we assumed everything was fine, it wasn't. After about 20 min of waiting for the next round of drinks that we had put in, we asked our server if our drinks were coming out soon. She informed us that the drink service had ended (at 830pm) and they were only offering tea. Other patrons in the restaurant were obviously still drinking and being served, so it felt very odd that we had not only been cut off from alcohol because of a clumsy mistake, but also being lied to about it. We didn't want to cause a scene so we didn't say anything but the rest of the meal and experience was very awkward after that and hard to enjoy. He kept coming over and making snarky comments to us while refilling our waters and we were all just quietly looking around at each other horrified and embarrassed, and trying to understand why he was being so rude to us. Then for one course towards the end, our server brought us each a small sips worth of wine. The restaurant manager came over and said "the chef INSISTED that wine be paired with this course" as if we were children that were being punished. It was SO STRANGE. At the end of the meal the chef came out of the kitchen to our table and apologized to us on behalf of the restaurant manager. He said the manager was upset because some of the wine had splashed on the fire centerpiece on the table. This was the first time anyone had explained to us what was going on and why we weren't being served, but at least we had answers. Also, if the manager thought I was drunk I would understand not serving me (even though I wasn't even close and had one sip of wine) but to cut off the entire table without disclosing why, and then being rude to us about it for the rest of dinner made the experience so unenjoyable. This also NEVER would've happened to us if we had been a table of all men, so it felt like a very sexist and unfair abuse of power. The chef coming to apologize on his behalf also confirms how insane this entire situation was, and the chef also tried to rectify the situation by asking if we wanted to get pictures in the kitchen with him and the sous chefs which was very kind of him. We still tipped outrageously/ as if the bill had drinks on it because it wasn't our servers fault and she was lovely and we could tell she felt bad for us. That being said I didn't want to leave a bad review because the chef and our server were both great and tried to rectify the situation as much as possible and the food was also good. But my friends and I still talk about how horrifying and upsetting this night was and I feel like if I was the owner I would want to know about this.

Dining environment: 

Delicious index: 

My sister and I said that my friend's store is very good, so I just came to try it when I was free. A 15 course course. Every dish is delicious and gives people a very amazing feeling. The restaurant is beautiful and the decoration style is very suitable for a date. And there are private rooms for multiple people.

The service staff is very caring, silently observing you, and appearing at the first time you need it, full of sense of security

Just exquisite... I think out of all the fine dining meals I have had in NYC, this is up there near the top. The chefs here treated all the ingredients with such care and I definitely noticed as a diner. 

As mentioned by many others, the menu is seafood focused, so please note that if you plan to eat here!

Service was of course amazing, worthy of the Michelin Star name.
Great service and creative dishes. Intimate and upscale setting. My husband took me here for my birthday and it was a great experience.

Food was on the salty side but presentation was 10/10. Make sure you are 30% full before dining as the portions are tiny. It was a good experience but I won't recommend it unless you just have to try a 2 star restaurant or love caviar. Service is 11/10.

One of my top picks for dining in New York. Every dish was outstanding and prepared to the highest level. The chef sources the finest ingredients from Scandinavia to the Northeastern region of the United States. The chef is a master of sauces and each dish was accompanied with a beautiful combination of of flavours and highlighted the meticulous technique of chef Berselius. Everyone who worked there was warm, friendly and knowledgeable. A very memorable meal.

Aska's TWO Star Michelin Chef Fredrik Berselius 

Deep in Williamsburg, Brooklyn I had experienced Stockholm-born Chef's take on New Nordic cuisine in an elegantly designed space with an open kitchen. It's in a tasting menu format that had at least three courses highlighting three kinds of top-end and rare caviar. One dish highlighted in-house dry-aged duck, another was the most delicious preparation of game meat I tried, medium rare venison topped topped with morel mushroom. We were served the best parts of specially sourced ocean meats such as langoustine, crab, lobster and scallops that came served with the Chef's myriad of sauces. 

People who lacks the temperament and appreciation for museums and curated collections will have a hard time understanding experiences like this.

Aska is clearly in the top 5 restaurant experiences of my life.  The staff are extremely knowledgeable and provided excellent service throughout the entire experience.  We enjoyed the 15 course tasting menu with wine pairings.   Both soms we interacted with provided us with great details on each wine pairing.  I will certainly recommend Aska to anyone traveling to NYC or BK.  Thanks for providing us with such a great experience!

Since my initial visit to Aska, I have visited three other times and somehow every experience has brought something new and impressive. The food continues to be the best I've had from any restaurant that I've been to. The service is impeccable, and the sommelier is a genius. Her ability to find incredible pairings to every dish is so admirable, and I love that she throws  curve balls to the typical wine combinations by adding a sake or two to the meal. Chef Berselius and his team just continue to elevate their creations every time too. The Chef has even been gracious enough to come chat with us, while remembering that my fiancee and I celebrated our engagement at the restaurant last year. Aska has geniunely become a happy place for us that we plan to return to yearly and I can't recommend it enough.

Absolutely incredible and very memorable dining experiences. If you're looking for some elegant, special, and fish-y, definitely check out Aska.

I came with my partner for a special birthday. We had the 15-course meal and wine pairing. Everything was really beautiful, even a small bite. You will definitely have enough food. Each bite was incredibly satiating, but you were also left wanting a little more. Thank goodness for the additional courses!

The vibe is dark, mysterious, and elegant. 

All of our servers were professional and friendly. I only wish I had been able to hear them when they presented the dishes a little more.

The wine pairing is definitely worth it and also very unique - some wines you'd never have discovered otherwise. 

Strong recommend.

Might be one of my favorite michelins yet. The food is spectacular, with a seafood focus, and all the flavors mesh together so well. The service is also quick, so you finish the meal as fast as you eat :) It was a bit noisy/hard to hear though due to the proximity of the tables. Overall though, very well worth the price with the quality of ingredients and the artfully crafted flavor profiles of each dish.

One of the best dining experiences I have ever had. From the quality of the food and ingredients. To the quality and experience of platting. All of the staff were amazing making sure we had an excellent time without an air of pretense which was appreciate. The all black interior is perfect making you focus in on the colors of the food. I highly recommend.

I had a lovely and memorable night at Aska.

The ambiance was elegant yet welcoming, making it a perfect place to celebrate a special occasion. The service was wonderful as the different chefs brings each dish to your table and guided us through the tasting menu. 

The innovative and seasonal menu was perfect for my taste buds. I love Scandinavian food as it is mostly seafood. I also recommend getting the wine pairing as it really paired well with the dishes (especially the sake)

I rate this spot 10/10! Every course was amazing, there were no misses. If you love seafood esp raw seafood, and caviar, this is the spot for you! 

Service is great, they were very attentive

This spot is also great for content. The lighting of this place is very well done. Love that everything in the restaurant was black while the table was lit up perfectly, so pictures of the food and of ourselves comes out looking great without having to use another light source.

My brother had his wedding dinner here in their private dining space. Impeccable service and food. Careful attention to food allergies. Engaging staff discussing everything you'd ask for. Perfect wine suggestions. 

I want to go back. Good lord.

I've spent an inordinate amount of time thinking about my meal at Aska. I hadn't had any exposure to Scandinavian food prior to this, and I'll be the first to admit that a 16 course tasting menu is not exactly a conventional introduction to a cuisine. And after one meal, I don't know whether I feel like I have the right to have an opinion on the food itself. It feels more complicated than simply judging whether I liked it or I didn't, and this is going to be the craziest food take, but I don't think it even remotely matters whether I liked it or not. 

After all this deliberation (and lots of conversations in my head about how much of a pretentious food snob I sound like, even to myself), the only conclusion I came to was that this meal is all about connection. I've never eaten a meal that felt so harmonious in its execution, from the aesthetic, to the ingredients, to the culinary techniques. You know that feeling you get when you look at a painting of the ocean and you can smell the seawater? Aska gives me similar vibes.

It's clear that Aska cares so much about how it artistically and faithfully represents Scandinavia, not just Scandinavian cuisine. Everything harkened back to Nordic nature, in both flavor and aesthetic, and that's what makes Aska so special. The first course was a dish that resembled a yellow wildflower native to Scandinavia, and tasted like the ocean waters that surround the region. So many dishes relied on delicate foams that reminded me of seafoam. And even preparations that weren't obvious homages to nature still made me feel connected to nature anyways. The demi-glace served with their quail, which was the result of hours of reduction of the quail bones themselves, felt like a refined version of something that was made in a Scandinavian cabin centuries ago. 

I don't think I'd rank Scandinavian cuisine as being one of my favorites. But Aska was one of the most pleasantly thought provoking experiences I've ever had. I've never quite experienced something that tied every aspect of food back to its culture with such reverence. And restaurants like Aska are what will always motivate me to try new cuisines and experience new food.

Aska's chef is Chef Berselius, and the cuisine focuses on the NE US region with Scandinavian influences.

There are only 10 tables per evening, so reservations can be somewhat difficult to obtain - the menu is a multi-course tasting menu, which includes about 12-14 courses with an optional wine pairing.

Our menu included:
+Sea Oak - with blue mussel emulsion
+Kohlrabi - kohlrabi compressed with linden leaf oil and linden flower vinegar
+Vendace - a small tart with vendace roe, marinated in horseradish oil and lilac vinegar
+Custard - creme royale with lobster claw, trout roe, and the essence of elderflower
+Caviar - kingfish from Denmark and osetra caviar from Madagascar with smoked eel, green gooseberry, and juniper
+Scallop - live scallop from Cape Cod with white turnips and black currant leaf
+Lobster - lobster tail from Maine with Kaluga caviar, wild carrot flower and white asparagus
+Trout - prepared with salted white currants
+Langoustine - grilled Langoustine tail from Norway with a caramelized shell and red gooseberry sauce
+Hake - tsar imperial beluga caviar, Swedish dark beer, and flowering dill
+Quail - roasted quail breast with wild leeks and black truffles and salted white truffle and black walnut sauce
+Venison - Millbrook venison with black sunchokes, hen of the woods, and a sweet bun
+Berries - tart prepared with preserved berries and woodruff
+Caramel - caramelized ice cream and almond tart
+Sorbet - milk sorbet with grass-fed cream and meadowsweet cordial
+Confections - rye leave & clover, canele & Swedish punsch, beet & black currant, salted licorice, and madeleine & sea buckthorn

Honestly, even though each course was well-presented, the focus seemed to be on the presentation rather than the flavors.  With the price point, we had higher expectations, considering.

Service was fine.

+underwhelming tasting menu

I had an entire hamburger right before this dinner and thought it was the perfect amount of food to eat after having a meal lol. If I hadn't eaten it I would've prob left hungry but since I did.. the meal was amazing and each dish was very unique. One star off because the timing was super slow (this is after we specifically asked them to speed it up since some people in our group didn't pre eat and were hungry, but they still went way over estimated time) 

Would love if they got a cocktail menu

Visited for lunch. There are plenty of street parking around. Just need to make sure you are not on cleaning time. There is an electric car charging station ~5 mins walk to south. 

The place was very modern. Staffs were very kind. Course menu, comes as you eat. They pace the servings depending on how fast you are eating. The foods were really good. Probably one of best fine dining. Although restaurant says Scandinavian, i felt like they are fusion restaurant.  All of the ingredients were fresh. Chefs come and explain each dish and also tell me where they were from.

Overall, i really enjoyed my visit here. Just one thing.. please dont hang coat on hook.. especially if they are in material that deforms easily like wool..
Aska deserves a 3-star (but I am partial to Scandinavian?). Their food is very elegant and pure, great wine list.

Came here for my husband's birthday and had a fantastic time. We enjoyed every course for the tasting. My husband had the wine pairing - it was pricey but worth it for a special occasion. They were detailed and patient explaining each pairing, the selection paired beautifully with each course and they were extremely generous with the pours. The meal placed a heavy emphasis on seafood and was perfectly executed. Flavors were balanced but deep - full of umami - while still maintaining a certain delicacy and lightness. Of the many Michelin starred restaurants, I found the atmosphere at Aska to be my favorite. It strikes a perfect blend of coziness while still allowing for privacy. Each table has enough space and room so that your party can be immersed in their own conversations while retaining a certain liveliness that comes with seeing people and tables close by. I also liked that tables all faced the kitchen so you're able to see the action. Lastly was the service which was impeccable but not stuffy or overly uptight. Highly recommend!

Had an outstanding meal here recently - stopped in for lunch with some friends. Service was amazing, the somm/wine director Missy was amazing, pacing of the meal was perfect, everyone was friendly and warm. And food was incredible.

Opening bites were all fun and interesting, well executed and gorgeous. The tarts here/croustades were so good, shells were the perfect texture. scallop, trout, and langoustine were all amazing - sauce on the langoustine dish was superb and the best I've had outside of scandinavia. main entrees, bread, pre dessert and desserts were all fantastic. lovely meal and will be returning hopefully sooner than later.

My Bestie with an impeccable pallet brought us here when we were in town and it was just out of this world amazing! 

Highly recommend to make reservations and treat yourself the ambiance and service is to the t! You will not be disappointed!

Incredible lunch tasting menu!! Their presentation is some of the best I've ever seen, with each plate or bowl being so unique and beautiful. We also loved the mocktail wine pairing. We've never seen this available before and love that more restaurants are making this an offering. 

The food was delicious but for the price, you could go to other Michelin star restaurants and find better. If your goal is beautiful food presentation this is definitely the place for it. 

I will call out one of the mocktails was so good we went out and bought it ourselves!!

A very pleasant night of birthday dinner here.

Mostly black and minimal interior space, maybe would appreciate a little upgrade for a 2-star restaurant. Would hope there's visibility to the sort-of-open-kitchen to chefs in actions.

It was a 13 courses dinner. Mostly very delicious lead to a happy tummy. Each courses was present with the main protein and spoon poured with rich and flavorful sauce created. Trout and Hake and ice cream dessert were slightly underwhelming. Other than that, def worth a try!!
Just very well done! Will be back. Everything from food to service was pleasant. Food was better than a few other similar two star places.

Absolutely amazing experience from start to finish. The vibe of the interior is very cool, the staff was attentive and friendly and not overbearing, and the food was some of the best food I have had in my life. Highly highly recommend

I came here on Mother's Day for the tasting menu with my mom and dad who are not super fancy people and they loved it! The service was so warm and attentive without being cloying. The food was excellent. The dessert course was probably my favorite- it made me feel like I was hanging out with the sugar plum fairy. All in all it was a memorable experience and my partner wants to go again in the near future because he loved it so much. Thank you for making my mom feel so special!
Very impressive and tasty 13 course tasting menu. All the dishes are very flavorful and extremely creative and pretty looking. The service is impeccable and very attentive!

4.5 would be more accurate, since not every aspect was magical. But as a Sunday lunch service, I was grateful they were even open. Their dinner service may be just slightly different, but I feel its going to cover the same ground. 

The amouse bouches were a seaweed chip with mustard, kohlrabi with pickled lingnon flowers, and a shrimp roe looking tart. All of them were delicious and should be savored slowly.  The first two don't even have fish in them, but they clearly resonate as fish. The kohlrabi especially played with my sight as it looked and felt like a filet of fish. 

The scallop wrapped in (don't remember what it was) with a caramelized scallop sauce was quite light, but there was a sense of serenity that followed it. The sauce is the true workhorse that has flavor for days. Overall it felt like a French onion soup, or should I say Fjord onion soup?!

The lobster dish take lobster to a while new level (for me at least) the stacking of textures is what really hits home with cascading layers of melting lobster flavor. The oil, curd, and foam all encapsulate the butter poached lobster beautifully, as if I'm eating a full brown chicken inside the proverbial yolk of an egg. The langoustine tail lacquered in a gooseberry glaze with gooseberry jam droplets and head stock evoked something in me that was carnal. The meal had been mostly relaxing, but something about this dish woke my ass up (in a good way). I thought the last lobster dish was amazing. And then this one came in and blew it away! The intense sauce and sweetness of the gooseberries are what really kick this into high gear. 

The white fish (fluke) with a bring, Bulgarian caviar with a dark swedish ale reduced into a syrup mixed with dill oil. This dish felt like it should have been presented before the lobster dishes for me personally. It was much was toned down compared to the last lobster dish. While the first few bites were unimpressive, the later half of the dish started to stand out more to me. Overall, it grew on my tongue as the sauce built a nice coating on my tongue. Using the briny caviar as a seasoning instead of salt was a great idea! 

Turbo fish with chamomile, turbo stock sauce with toasted hay, pickled white beets. This also doesn't boom with flavor initially, but grows in intensity like appearing from a foggy marsh. The chamomile and toasted hay combo is genius! Like an ivory and ebony collaboration of this smoke feel. They also cut the beets in this fun way that look like plastic cutouts for a plastic train set. 

Preserved gooseberry tart with woodruff oil was so damn satisfying. I could have eaten a dozen of these! It may have been one of the best palate cleansers I've had 

The ice cream was OK, but it didn't pop as much as I would had hoped. But it was still refreshing with how hot it was outside. 

The three spirit non alcoholic offerings were fantastic! It feels abrasive like a cold wind, but the sweet, botanical aromas swirl around in a delightful carousel of an aftertaste. The nightcap was so good I ended up buying a bottle for myself once I got back home!

Service wise was what I would expect from a Michelin establishment. Probably because of my demeanor and keen eye for detail, the service crew felt quite relaxed and casual with me. It helps that most of the servers were near my age and had similar interest in the food and drinks I was consuming.

4 courses were some of the best dishes I've ever had:
1. The hake (a fish similar to cod) topped with caviar sitting in a creamy sauce with Swedish dark beer and flowering dill. The hake was so tender and flaky. The sauce was so rich and creamy, but the dark beer and dill added a subtle but immense depth to the flavor
2. The langoustine grilled and accompanied by a sauce of the caramelized shell and droplets of gooseberry. The langoustine was so tender and full of umami, and the grill on top added a satisfying crunch. The sauce was again so creamy, but the droplets of gooseberry added an explosion of flavor that perfectly elevates the langoustine.
3. The custard with lobster in a foam that is like eating a fluffy, bubbly cloud. There was a savory oil with cheese at the bottom which was so buttery. There were bits of crunchy vegetables and roe to add varying elements of taste and texture and balance the richness.
4. Caviar on top of king fish and eel in a creamy mayo. The umami from this is truly unbeatable, and everything just blends together to make a harmonious bite. There is a nice seaweed-like shell that perfectly holds this bite and gives a nice crisp.

Unfortunately, the rest of courses were unremarkable. The seafood was cooked beautifully, but the flavors felt a little flat. This place does seafood significantly better than meat (as indicated by the final two savory courses of quail). The bread with malted barley and pine mushroom butter was amazing though, the bread was buttery and fragrant and the mushroom gave the butter such an interesting earthiness and umami.

The desserts were also disappointing, not one of those beautiful and creative desserts that you'd expect at such a high-end restaurant. For instance, milk sorbet on cream is so milky, albeit this place does love  rich and creamy flavors.

The portions are also kinda small, we were expecting a bigger main course and dessert as a finale to each part of the meal, but that never came.

However, those 4 courses are truly divine and make up for everything and carry the meal so hard to the well deserved 5/5!

Huge shoutout to the service here too, the waiters (and it seems like the chefs themselves were serving too) were so attentive. They even printed out the special menu at the end for someone dining with us with dietary restrictions.

A top notch experience and definitely in my top Michelin star meals! 

We started off at the back "garden" of the restaurant where we had some snacks and welcome champagne. We then moved into the main dining hall which was small but cozy. We saw the head chef as well in the kitchen. 

If you love seafood, this is definitely the place to go! All the dishes were innovative and fresh, and the wine pairing was excellent with the sommelier even giving us another taste of sake as we talked to her.

Would highly recommend trying Aska for a great experience.
Delicious food and gorgeous presentation! We came for a birthday celebration and had a great time.

A Journey of Nostalgia and Innovation at Aska

Dining at Aska, a Michelin 2-star gem in Brooklyn, is nothing short of a culinary voyage. Our evening began with an adventurous subway ride from Central Park to Brooklyn, anticipating the seafood-focused tasting menu that awaited us. From the very first bite, Aska took us on a journey not only of taste but also of memory.

 The scallop dish was a perfect example of this. Thinly sliced and delicately rolled around a stick of turnip, the scallops floated in a lightly sauced Japanese-inspired broth. What stood out was the subtle radish note in the broth, transporting me back fifty years to a village outing where fresh turnip soup nourished middle school children after a day of helping farmers. Sweet, bitter, and comforting, the dish held within it a quiet complexity that lingered with each sip.

 Next came finely chopped lobster paired with carrots and asparagus, nestled under a frothy foam with a subtly sweet and acidic sauce. The combination of the lobster's silky texture and the crispness of the vegetables created a playful contrast that was satisfying yet elegant. As the tasting menu continued, dishes of trout, langoustine, hake, and caviar were beautifully executed, each showcasing the freshness and depth of east coast seafood.

 But it was the transition to the quail dish that surprised and delighted me. The quail breast, cleverly shaped like quail eggs, was served alongside cauliflower and a rich brown sauce made from the quail's thighs and legs. This dish offered a shift from the oceanic to the earthy, providing a savory, comforting close to our seafood-centric experience.

 Asks's tasting menu weaves together innovation with personal nostalgia, creating an unforgettable dining experience. The balance of flavors, textures, and presentation reflects not only technical mastery but also a deep understanding of how food connects us to memory. For those seeking more than just a meal, Aska offers a sensory journey that lingers well beyond the final course.

This restaurant has been on my list for the longest time and it was absolutely worth the wait! To me, it was a 3 Michelin Star experience and genuinely one of my top meals. My partner surprised me on my birthday with a dinner here and the staff was definitely prepared. Special shout out to Nico who was our sommelier and to the rest of the staff who just took such great care of the restaraunt and their guests. 

This was a 14 course menu and Nico helped me find a drink I could enjoy. At first, I was hesitant since I am a bit picky and not very knowledgable in drinks but I told him my flavor preferences and he managed to find a drink that matched it and offered me to try it. I was just really impressed by his depth of knowledge and even told us which course to best have it with. 

This restaurant honeslty blew my mind with their creativity and flavors. I think that it really pushed the boundaries of flavors that I never knew was possible but at the same time, some of them tasted so familiar. I hope they don't find this offensive because I mean this is in the best way possible, but they had this sauce that they were using throughout the menu in various versions, but sometimes it reminded me of McDonalds, and it was so addicting. 

It's so difficult to choose my favorite dish of the night, there were so many. One of my top dishes was the Caviar dish (king fish, smoked eel, and caviar) and it was one of the appetizers that was wrapped in seaweed I think. The sauce they used for some reason reminded me of a pork floss bun from a Chinese bakery, and specifically the mayo sauce. I wanted to eat it again and experience it all over for the first time again. 

The chefs also came by to explain the dishes which I thought was really intimate and wonderful. You could really tell how passionate and proud they were and I would get really excited to try every dish. I am also a big seafood lover so the fact that the entire menu was basically seafood did make it even better. There was this pine mushroom dish that fascinated me. It was so beautiful and I honeslty didn't know it was a meat dish. They somehow managed to wrap a quail leg with mushroom. Another top dish for me was their langoustine. Again, that suace they used - just magnificent. 

I could go on and on about every single dish honestly, but truly it's a one of a kind experience and I plan to return someday. Everything was amazing from the service, the decor, the food, and their garden in the back! I wanted more of everything I had and my partner and I just could not stop raving about the food. They also knew it was my birthday and made a point to wish me birthday wishes and had a little dessert cake for me and I was so happy to have celebrated here. 

Thank you to all the staff and chefs at Aska! I hope to return soon!

I would have never considered coming to a restaurant like this on my own, only because I personally have a hard time justifying spending more than a certain amount of money on a meal, but I was lucky enough to go last night with my partner and his mom to celebrate his birthday. The food was beautiful, inventive, and delicious--so much complex flavor. By the end of the 12 courses not only was I stuffed, but my partner, who I sometimes suspect has a bottomless stomach, was. The tiny portions of each course made a lot of sense to me; several were so rich (in a good way) that you wouldn't be able to eat a larger portion. The service was also incredible, and everyone working was paying attention to every detail, down to the woman who saw me head to the bathroom when it was already occupied and ushered me to another one downstairs so I wouldn't have to wait. Everything inside is black and dark, which I think helps you focus more on the food. I now understand why people are willing to spend $$$ on a meal when it is this good. I would consider coming back in the future to celebrate a special occasion.

This was a fantastic tasting menu experience. There were 12-15 courses and maybe 10 of dishes were seafood, and what was surprising was that each one was so different from the others. Each one has different textures, flavors, and composition, and was truly creative. The chefs prep the dishes in an open kitchen and bring it to you, with a story of all of the components. 

One minor qualm is that each dish was soo small, and by the end I was hoping for a heartier dish. Still, overall fantastic place!

I've been to the majority of the 'fancy' restaurants in NYC and can safely say our experience at Aska was the best we've had. Whether it was one of the multiple dishes garnished with caviar, the beautifully poached langoustine or the exquisitely cooked Hake or any of the rare wines we were served I could not rave about this experience more. Massive shoutout to Nico, Missy, Isaac, Juan, and Emma. Cannot wait to be back!
